Customer Relations Representative – Customer & Dealership Support

About the Role

As a Customer Relations Representative, you will play an important role in creating positive experiences for automotive customers and dealership teams. Our team partners closely with dealerships while serving as a resource for customers who need assistance with questions, concerns, and issues related to their vehicle ownership experience.

You will listen to customer concerns, research available solutions, provide knowledgeable guidance, and work with dealership personnel when additional support or coordination is needed.

This is a great opportunity for someone who enjoys helping people, solving problems, learning about automotive technology, and making complicated situations easier for customers. Every interaction is an opportunity to build trust and help create a positive experience.

What You'll Do

  • Customer Interaction: Engage with customers by answering incoming calls, listening carefully to their questions or concerns, and providing professional, empathetic, and timely assistance.

  • Customer Advocacy: Take ownership of customer concerns and work to understand the situation from the customer's perspective while helping identify the best available path toward resolution.

  • Dealership Partnership: Work collaboratively with dealerships to help address customer concerns, provide guidance, and coordinate information when dealership involvement is needed.

  • Problem Resolution: Research customer concerns, determine appropriate solutions, and follow through to help ensure issues are addressed effectively and efficiently.

  • Recall & Customer Support Program Assistance: Provide customers and dealership personnel with guidance related to vehicle recalls and Customer Support Programs, including helping explain available resources and next steps.

  • Warranty Support: Assist with questions related to warranty parameters and dealership processes, helping customers better understand their options while partnering with dealerships when necessary.

  • Connected Services Support: Assist customers with connected services enrollment, connectivity questions, and troubleshooting. Help customers navigate technology-related concerns and provide clear instructions for available solutions.

  • Technical Assistance: Provide support for in-vehicle technology, including phone pairing, multimedia systems, navigation, and other connected vehicle features.

  • Research & Investigation: Utilize internal systems, online resources, reference materials, and available tools to research unique or complex customer concerns and identify accurate, appropriate solutions.

  • Multi-Tasking Excellence: Navigate multiple software applications and systems while actively listening to customers, documenting information, researching concerns, and communicating solutions.

  • Dealership Coordination: When a customer concern requires dealership involvement, work with the appropriate dealership contacts to help facilitate communication and support a successful customer outcome.

  • Escalation Assistance: Recognize concerns that require additional review or support and follow established escalation procedures while maintaining ownership of the customer experience.

  • Clear Communication: Explain processes, technical information, and next steps in a clear and easy-to-understand manner, adapting your communication style to meet each customer's needs.

  • Emotional Intelligence: Use empathy, patience, and professionalism when interacting with customers who may be frustrated, confused, or experiencing a challenging situation.

  • Customer Experience: Look for opportunities to make each interaction easier and more positive. Your goal is not simply to answer a question, but to ensure the customer feels heard, supported, and confident about their next steps.

  • Accuracy & Attention to Detail: Accurately document customer interactions, follow established procedures, and ensure information is handled consistently and appropriately.

  • Attendance & Punctuality: Maintain excellent attendance and punctuality to provide reliable and consistent support to our customers and dealership partners.

What We're Looking For

Customer Service & Communication

  • A strong communicator who can build rapport and trust with customers and dealership personnel.

  • A compassionate and patient problem solver who can listen to a customer's concern and identify the best way to help.

  • Comfortable working with technology and learning new software applications and systems.

  • Able to research information independently and use available resources to find solutions.

  • Detail-oriented and organized, with the ability to manage multiple systems and priorities at the same time.

  • Comfortable working in a fast-paced customer service environment where every interaction may bring a different question or challenge.

  • Able to remain calm, professional, and solution-focused when working with frustrated or emotional customers.

  • Confident working independently while also knowing when to collaborate with teammates or escalate a concern.

  • Dependable, accountable, and committed to providing consistent support.

  • Motivated by the opportunity to make a difference in someone's experience.

  • Extremely detailed oriented to ensure accurate information is being relayed to the customer.

Resilience & Coachability

  • Ability to remain composed and productive during high-volume periods and challenging customer interactions.

  • Open to frequent feedback, coaching, and performance discussions.

  • Demonstrates accountability for individual results.

  • Willing and able to adjust behaviors based on coaching and performance feedback.

  • Maintains a positive, professional approach when priorities or expectations change.

Remote Work Discipline

  • Ability to work independently in a structured remote contact center environment.

  • Strong time-management and organizational skills.

  • Ability to consistently meet attendance, schedule, quality, and performance expectations.

  • Ability to maintain a professional, distraction-free workspace while working.

  • Dependable and prepared to begin work and return from scheduled breaks at assigned times.

What You’ll Receive

  • Competitive Pay: $16 per hour ($15 base pay + $1 bilingual Spanish premium), with opportunities for performance-based incentives.

  • Comprehensive Benefits: Medical, dental, and vision insurance options.

  • Paid Training: Comprehensive training designed to prepare you for success in the role.

  • Referral for Life Program: Opportunities to earn ongoing referral bonuses for eligible employee referrals.

  • Career Growth: Opportunities for advancement, professional development, and leadership career pathways.

  • Supportive Remote Environment: A collaborative virtual team focused on continuous learning, development, and success.

  • Inclusive Culture: VXI is an Equal Opportunity Employer, including individuals with disabilities and veterans.

Why You’ll Love Working Here

At VXI, we recognize that great customer experiences start with great people. You’ll be part of a team that values customer connection, empathy, accountability, continuous learning, and personal growth.

This is an opportunity to strengthen your customer service, communication, critical-thinking, problem-solving, and relationship-building skills while developing a career in a fast-paced customer experience environment.

Every customer interaction is an opportunity to make a difference. Whether you’re answering a question, resolving a concern, helping with an order, or supporting a frustrated customer, your goal is to ensure the customer feels heard, valued, and confident in the path forward.

If you enjoy connecting with people, solving problems, taking ownership, and creating exceptional experiences, we’d love to hear from you.

Apply today to join VXI as a Customer Service Advisor and help us create extraordinary customer experiences.

If you like wild growth and working with happy, enthusiastic over-achievers, you'll enjoy your career with us!

• High School Diploma

Right now, all of the Founder's scheduling, follow-up tracking, and day-to-day operational memory rides on his own bandwidth — and that doesn't scale as the organization's donor, partner, and fellow relationships grow. This role exists to take real ownership of the calendar, the inbox, and the "did we follow up with X" loop, using Claude and Claude Code/CLI as core working tools rather than optional add-ons. jobs.description:
GitLab is the intelligent orchestration platform for DevSecOps. GitLab enables organizations to increase developer productivity, improve operational efficiency, reduce security and compliance risk, and accelerate digital transformation. More than 50 million registered users and more than 50% of the Fortune 100* trust GitLab to ship better, more secure software faster.

The same principles built into our products are reflected in how our team works: we embrace AI as a core productivity multiplier, with all team members expected to incorporate AI into their daily workflows to drive efficiency, innovation, and impact. GitLab is where careers accelerate, innovation flourishes, and every voice is valued. Our high-performance culture is driven by our values and continuous knowledge exchange, enabling our team members to reach their full potential while collaborating with industry leaders to solve complex problems. Co-create the future with us as we build technology that transforms how the world develops software.

*Fortune 500® is a registered trademark of Fortune Media IP Limited, used under license. Claim based on GitLab data. Fortune 100 refers to the top 20% ranked companies in the 2025 Fortune 500 list, published in June 2025. Fortune and Fortune Media IP Limited are not affiliated with, and do not endorse products or services of GitLab.

An overview of this role

GitLab's Security Risk function is responsible for reducing risk across the security division: third-party risk (TPRM), annual security risk assessments, quarterly risk reporting, and remediation of security findings. As a Senior Security Risk Engineer, you'll take ownership of risk identification, quantification, and remediation tracking across the business, and you'll be a driving force behind automating and modernizing how the team does this work using AI and scripting. Reporting to the Security Risk Manager, you will bring expertise on risk methodology, risk-based thinking, and AI-enablement.

In this role, you'll partner closely with Security, Legal, IT, Product, and Engineering to translate technical findings and vendor risk into business-relevant risk statements and risk treatments. You’ll help surface emerging risks, and report top risks to leadership.

Some examples of our projects:

  • Building and maintaining a risk register that translates technical vulnerabilities, control gaps, and third-party risk findings into quantified, business-relevant risk statements.
  • Driving cross-functional remediation of security findings and risk issues to closure, tracked against SLAs.
  • Driving automation and AI-enabled improvements for risk and GRC workflows so the team can spend less time on manual work and more time on high-value risk analysis and program maturity.

What you'll do

  • Own risk identification, analysis, and prioritization across third-party risk (TPRM), security risk assessments, and security findings, using an established risk framework (e.g., NIST RMF, ISO 31000, or NIST 800-39).
  • Translate technical vulnerabilities, control gaps, and risk findings into clear, quantified risk statements that non-security stakeholders and leadership can act on.
  • Drive remediation of findings and risk exceptions to closure, partnering with Engineering, IT, Product, and Legal, and escalating stalled or high-severity items.
  • Mature and maintain a risk register and quarterly reporting cadence that gives leadership clear visibility into open risk, remediation progress, and trends.
  • Own and mature AI risk management, including AI impact assessments, AI risk assessments, and risk treatments, to support ISO 42001 certification.
  • Design, develop, and implement key risk indicators and supporting metrics for top risks in the risk register.
  • Identify manual, repetitive steps in risk and TPRM workflows and personally build the automation, scripting, or AI-enabled tooling to remove them.
  • Contribute to the roadmap for the risk program, incorporating new frameworks, regulatory changes, and lessons learned from past assessments.
  • Monitor the internal and external risk landscape (new frameworks, threat trends, business changes) to identify and escalate emerging risks before they become findings.

What you'll bring

  • 5+ years of experience in security risk management, working with security-centric risk management or compliance frameworks (e.g., NIST RMF, NIST 800-39, ISO 31000). Familiarity with AI governance frameworks (e.g., ISO 42001, NIST AI RMF) is a plus.
  • Experience designing and executing qualitative and quantitative risk analyses that translate technical risks into measurable business impact.
  • A track record of driving risk assessments, risk registers, and remediation efforts to closure across IT, Procurement, Internal Audit, Legal, Product, and Engineering, in a heavily regulated or multi-entity environment.
  • Experience interpreting technical control requirements and translating them for both technical and non-technical stakeholders.
  • Demonstrated bias toward automation: you've personally built scripts, workflows, or AI-enabled tooling that reduced manual risk or GRC work, not just evaluated tools conceptually.
  • Comfort operating with ambiguity, managing multiple concurrent assessments, and reprioritizing under tight deadlines.
  • Exceptional written and verbal communication skills with demonstrated ability to translate security risks into business risks.
  • Strong understanding of cloud security, SaaS security models, and DevSecOps practices.
  • Relevant certifications (e.g., CISSP, CISM, CISA, CRISC) are preferred but not required.

About the team

The Security Assurance organization helps GitLab build and maintain trust by strengthening how we approach security, compliance, and risk across the company. The Security Risk team sits within that group and owns third-party risk (TPRM), security risk assessments, and remediation of security findings. The Security Risk Team performs thorough, collaborative, and efficient risk assessments as well as drive risk reduction so that GitLab can achieve its goals while maintaining a high level of security. Security Risk counterparts are Security Compliance, Security Governance and Security Enablement functions.

jobs.description:
• Remote / flexible location in the SE Asia and Pacific region, with a preference for candidates based in Australia, PNG, Fiji, Timor Leste or Solomon Islands.
  • Part-time/4 days a week, fixed term contract for 24 months
  • Reports to Catalpa Director

Catalpa in a nutshell

Catalpa International is a global development organisation designing new, creative ways of tackling complex problems. We integrate international development practice, design thinking, and adaptive management with the potential of technology to drive change.

Our team is an eclectic bunch. We have designers, engineers, education specialists, international development practitioners, program people, operations people and plenty of people who don't fit neatly into any particular box! We work across different countries, cultures, disciplines and time zones — and we like it that way. Our work is one of a kind and honestly, pretty cool! Check us out at

Help us find, shape and win the work that matters

Catalpa is looking for an experienced Business Development Lead to help shape the next chapter of our growth.

This isn't a role for someone who just wants to manage tender calendars and chase people for proposal inputs. We're looking for someone who gets genuinely interested in an opportunity — who wants to understand the problem behind it, figure out where Catalpa could add something valuable, bring the right people into the conversation and help turn a good idea into a compelling proposition.

You'll work closely with our Directors and technical and program teams across the Asia-Pacific, helping us identify opportunities earlier, build stronger relationships with clients and partners, and develop brilliant proposals for work we're excited to do.

And yes, there will still be deadlines, compliance matrices and the occasional frantic final proposal check. It is business development, after all ;-)

So, what would you actually do?

You'll have a pretty broad remit, but your job essentially comes down to this: Help Catalpa find the right opportunities, position ourselves well and put forward excellent responses. That means you'll:

  • keep a close eye on what's coming — across donor and government pipelines, procurement portals, country strategies, sector priorities and our networks
  • help us identify opportunities early rather than waiting for a tender to land in someone's inbox
  • research clients, partners, markets and competitors and turn that information into useful insights
  • work with our technical and program teams to understand problems and shape potential responses
  • help us make sensible go/no-go decisions about where we invest our time and energy
  • build and maintain relationships with clients, partners, governments, consultants and other organisations across the region
  • lead priority proposals from early positioning through to submission
  • write, edit and shape complex technical content into clear, persuasive proposals
  • make sure our submissions are compliant, polished, on-brand and — importantly — submitted on time
  • help us better tell the Catalpa story through capability statements, case studies, pitch decks and other useful content; and
  • keep improving how we do business development, including finding sensible ways to use AI and digital tools to make the whole process smarter and more efficient.

A detailed Terms of Reference can be found here.

Requirements

Who are we looking for?
We're less interested in finding someone who ticks every imaginable BD box and more interested in finding someone with the judgement, experience and curiosity to do this role really well.

  • Experience working with government, bilateral or multilateral development partners or other institutional clients will be important, as is experience in international development and the Asia-Pacific - experience working with DFAT and/or MFAT opportunities would definitely get our attention.
  • You'll probably have around 5+ years of relevant experience across business development, partnerships, proposal development, international development or a related field.
  • You'll have managed significant tenders, proposals or funding submissions and know what it takes to get a complex response from “should we go for this?” to “submitted!”

But experience alone isn't really what will make this role work.

You'll probably thrive at Catalpa if you...

  • Have good BD judgement - You can look at an opportunity, ask smart questions and form a view about whether — and how — we should pursue it.
  • Can really write - You can take complicated technical thinking and turn it into something clear, persuasive and human. You're equally comfortable shaping a strategy, drafting a response, editing someone else's technical content or diving into tender requirements.
  • Like connecting people and ideas - You enjoy building relationships and bringing different people together around an opportunity.
  • Can see the big picture without losing the details - One minute you might be discussing Catalpa's positioning in a market; the next you're checking whether somebody's CV meets a tender requirement.
  • Are curious - You like getting underneath a new problem, understanding a client or sector and working out what really matters.
  • Can create order without creating bureaucracy - You're organised and you know how to keep a complicated proposal moving — but you don't need a 17-step process for everything.
  • Are comfortable when things aren't completely mapped out - Some opportunities start with a tender document. Others start with a conversation, a relationship or half an idea. You're comfortable working with both.
  • Care about the work behind the win - Growth matters to us because it allows Catalpa to keep doing meaningful work. We want someone who understands the commercial side of business development without losing sight of the social impact we're here to create.
  • Strong cultural competency and demonstrated ability to work effectively in diverse cultural contexts is a must.

What would success look like?

We won't be measuring success simply by counting how many tenders you submit. We'd love to see a healthier and more strategically aligned pipeline, stronger early relationships with priority clients and partners, better decisions about the opportunities we pursue, consistently excellent proposals and much better organisational knowledge about what we've done and what we can offer.

And ultimately? More great work that contributes to Catalpa's impact and long-term sustainability.

A few practical things

  • This is a part-time four-day-per-week role offered on a 24-month fixed-term contract.
  • We're a remote organisation, so the role has some flexibility around location. We're particularly interested in hearing from people based in Australia, Papua New Guinea, Fiji, Timor-Leste or Solomon Islands, where we have staffing hubs although we'll consider other locations within the Southeast Asia and Pacific region.
  • You'll report to our Catalpa Director and work closely with people right across the organisation.
  • Relevant tertiary qualifications in areas such as international development, business, communications or public policy are useful, but they're not essential.
  • What matters most is whether you've got the experience, judgement and way of working to make a real contribution.

Eligibility

We love working with kind, smart people from diverse backgrounds willing to learn new things. This job will require many skills, but feel free to apply even if you think you may not be a ‘perfect fit’.

Work environment

We work in a creative, supportive environment with colleagues from diverse walks of life, and we value their perspectives. We pay attention to the details and work together to achieve the best outcomes for our communities. Importantly, we work here because we love what we do and the impact we have.

We recognise that consultants balance a range of professional and personal commitments. We support flexible, remote ways of working and focus on outcomes rather than fixed schedules. We believe people do their best work when they have the space to take care of themselves, their families, and their communities. Help build, support and operate technology used by more than 8,000 organizations in over 100 countries – moving AI from possibility to production in real-world enterprise environments every day.


Role Overview

At Genesys, we help organizations create better customer and employee experiences through AI-powered experience orchestration. Our platform connects people, systems, data, and AI to deliver personalized experiences, automate complex business processes, and improve operational efficiency.

We are looking for a Principal Software Engineer with deep, hands-on Genesys Cloud experience to design and build the next generation of AI-powered applications and industry solutions on the Genesys Cloud platform.

This is a highly technical, hands-on engineering role. The ideal candidate combines deep Genesys Cloud engineering expertise with hands-on experience building advanced conversational or agentic AI applications using Genesys AI, Cognigy, Sierra, Decagon, Kore.ai, or similar platforms.

The ideal candidate has extensive experience developing applications and integrations on Genesys Cloud and understands how to combine Genesys Cloud APIs, Architect, AI capabilities, experience orchestration, data, and enterprise systems to create production-grade solutions.

A major focus of this role will be translating industry-specific business processes and customer challenges into reusable AI solutions. You will build AI applications, Digital Teammates, solution accelerators, and industry solutions for areas such as financial services, healthcare, insurance, retail, travel and hospitality, telecommunications, and the public sector.

You will work closely with Product, Engineering, Innovations, customers, and partners to turn emerging Genesys AI capabilities, external AI technologies, and industry requirements into scalable, repeatable, and productized solutions that can be deployed across multiple customers.

Key Responsibilities

  • Design and build production-grade applications and industry solutions on Genesys Cloud, leveraging Genesys Cloud APIs, SDKs, events, integrations, AI capabilities, and platform services.
  • Develop AI-powered customer and employee applications using Genesys Cloud AI capabilities, including AI Studio, Virtual Agent/Agentic Virtual Agent capabilities, Copilot, Architect, knowledge, and Experience Orchestration.
  • Translate industry-specific business processes and use cases into scalable AI applications, combining Genesys Cloud capabilities with enterprise systems, data, knowledge, AI models, and agentic technologies.
  • Build reusable industry solution accelerators, Digital Teammates, AI agents, workflows, and application components that can be configured and deployed across multiple customers within an industry.
  • Develop industry solutions addressing complex business challenges across financial services, healthcare, insurance, retail, travel and hospitality, telecommunications, and public sector environments.
  • Design sophisticated Genesys Architect flows and orchestration patterns across voice, digital, AI, workflows, data, and enterprise applications.
  • Build integrations using Genesys Cloud Platform APIs, Data Actions, event-driven architectures, webhooks, and external APIs.
  • Integrate Genesys Cloud with industry and enterprise platforms such as Salesforce, ServiceNow, Microsoft, AWS, CRM, ITSM, ERP, knowledge, healthcare, financial services, and workflow platforms.
  • Build agentic applications and multi-agent workflows where AI agents can reason, retrieve information, invoke tools and APIs, execute business processes, and collaborate with human employees.
  • Apply modern conversational and agentic AI patterns learned from platforms such as Genesys AI, Cognigy, Sierra, Decagon, Kore.ai, and similar technologies to build differentiated solutions on Genesys Cloud.
  • Design AI applications that combine LLMs, enterprise knowledge, tool/API calling, workflow orchestration, business rules, and enterprise systems of record.
  • Create reusable solution patterns that encapsulate industry workflows, business rules, integrations, AI capabilities, and best practices, accelerating time to value for customers.
  • Work with industry experts, customers, Product, and Engineering teams to identify high-value use cases and convert them into repeatable, productized solutions.
  • Build prototypes and MVPs using emerging Genesys Cloud AI and other AI technologies and rapidly convert successful concepts into scalable, production-ready industry applications.
  • Design applications for enterprise-scale requirements including security, reliability, observability, scalability, performance, compliance, and governance.
  • Provide technical leadership, architecture guidance, code reviews, and mentorship while remaining a hands-on builder and contributor.

Required Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Artificial Intelligence, or a related technical discipline.
  • 10+ years of software engineering, application development, or solution architecture experience.
  • 5+ years of hands-on Genesys Cloud experience, including designing, developing, integrating, and deploying applications on the platform.
  • Deep understanding of Genesys Cloud architecture, APIs, Architect, routing, conversations, integrations, Data Actions, and event-driven capabilities.
  • Strong hands-on experience developing enterprise applications using modern programming languages such as Python, JavaScript/TypeScript, Java, or similar technologies.
  • Experience building AI-powered applications, conversational AI solutions, virtual agents, or agentic applications using enterprise AI platforms and modern AI technologies.
  • Strong understanding of modern AI architectures including LLMs, RAG, AI agents, tool calling, orchestration, multi-agent systems, conversational AI, and agentic workflows.
  • Demonstrated experience building reusable enterprise or industry solutions, rather than only one-off customer implementations.
  • Experience translating complex industry business processes and use cases into technical architectures and production applications.
  • Experience building applications using REST APIs, SDKs, webhooks, event streams, microservices, and cloud-native architectures.
  • Experience integrating Genesys Cloud with enterprise applications such as CRM, ITSM, ERP, knowledge, and workflow platforms.
  • Experience translating AI capabilities into production-grade applications and reusable solutions, including integrations with enterprise APIs, knowledge systems, workflows, and business applications.
  • Experience taking solutions from prototype/MVP through production deployment and operation.
  • Demonstrated ability to provide technical leadership while remaining deeply involved in architecture, design, coding, prototyping, debugging, and implementation.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Hands-on experience with Genesys Cloud AI capabilities, including AI Studio, Virtual Agent/Agentic Virtual Agent, Copilot, Predictive Engagement, knowledge capabilities, and Experience Orchestration.
  • Hands-on experience building production AI applications using Cognigy, Sierra, Decagon, Kore.ai, or similar enterprise conversational and agentic AI platforms.
  • Experience developing custom applications and reusable solutions using the Genesys Cloud Developer Platform and APIs.
  • Experience with Genesys Cloud CX voice and digital channels, including routing, Architect flows, bots, messaging, and agent experiences.
  • Experience designing AI agents that combine conversational intelligence, reasoning, knowledge retrieval, tool/API calling, workflow orchestration, and business-process execution.
  • Experience building agentic AI applications that integrate LLMs with enterprise APIs, knowledge systems, CRM/ITSM platforms, workflow engines, and other systems of record.
  • Experience designing or developing industry-specific AI applications and reusable solution accelerators for financial services, healthcare, insurance, retail, telecommunications, travel and hospitality, or public sector.
  • Understanding of industry-specific business processes, regulatory requirements, data models, and enterprise application ecosystems.
  • Familiarity with AI development and orchestration frameworks such as LangChain, Semantic Kernel, AutoGen, CrewAI, or similar technologies.
  • Experience with cloud platforms such as AWS, Azure, or Google Cloud, including AI services such as Amazon Bedrock.
  • Experience with enterprise platforms such as Salesforce, ServiceNow, Microsoft Dynamics, or similar ecosystems.
  • Experience taking AI applications from prototype through enterprise production, including security, scalability, observability, governance, and reliability.
  • Experience working in innovation teams, rapid prototyping environments, or customer co-creation programs.

What Success Looks Like

Success in this role means being able to take an industry business problem or use case and rapidly turn it into a working, production-quality AI application built on Genesys Cloud.

More importantly, the goal is not simply to solve the problem for one customer. You will identify the common business process, integrations, AI capabilities, and orchestration patterns and turn them into a reusable industry solution that can be deployed across many customers.

You should be equally comfortable understanding an industry business process, discussing architecture, working with Genesys Cloud APIs, designing an Architect flow, writing application code, integrating enterprise systems, connecting AI models and agents, implementing tool/API calling, debugging interactions, and demonstrating the finished solution to customers and executives.

You should also be able to bring experience and architectural patterns from leading conversational and agentic AI platforms and apply those concepts effectively within the Genesys Cloud ecosystem.

This is not a traditional high-level architecture role. We are looking for a hands-on Principal Engineer who knows Genesys Cloud deeply and can combine its AI, orchestration, API, and integration capabilities with modern agentic AI technologies to build the next generation of AI-powered industry solutions.

jobs.title: Senior Director, Utility Strategy and Market Design
jobs.excerpt: The RoleFollowing Madison’s groundbreaking Community Infrastructure announcement to develop 1 GW and mobilize up to $2 billion in capital, we are hiring a leader to own MEI’s relationships with utilities, ISOs/RTOs, and state utility regulators.
jobs.description:
The Role

Following Madison’s groundbreaking Community Infrastructure announcement to develop 1 GW and mobilize up to $2 billion in capital, we are hiring a leader to own MEI’s relationships with utilities, ISOs/RTOs, and state utility regulators. This person will be critical in helping MEI shape the market rules and utility programs that determine whether distributed storage and solar can be interconnected, accredited, and compensated at the massive scale our plan requires.

This person will own MEI’s influence in those proceedings — identifying which rules actually matter to our thesis, deciding where our effort is best spent, and working directly with utilities and commission staff to craft programs that work for the utility, the Digital Infrastructure Partners, the community, and MEI at the same time.

This is a utility- and regulator-facing role, not a legislative one. A separate hire will own policy and government relations — legislative advocacy, executive branch engagement, and trade association strategy. The external counterparts for this role are the utility resource planner, the distribution engineer, the DER program manager, the commission staffer, and the ISO stakeholder committee: the people who design programs and write rules. The two roles will coordinate closely, but the mandate here is technical, program-level, and commercial.

This person will own MEI’s assessment of market and interconnection viability — verifying that the ISO, RTO, and utility will allow us to interconnect and provide capacity in a given location, now or on a known timeline, and building the path to change that where they will not. That assessment directly determines where MEI commits development capital, so the rigor and honesty of this work matters.

This role is ideal for someone who understands how utilities and their regulators make decisions — who has worked inside a rate case, a distribution plan, or a DER program design — and is ready to apply that experience directly. Credibility with utility and commission counterparts, and sound judgment about where to focus effort, are the core assets.

Responsibilities

  • Decide which dockets, filings, rulemakings, and stakeholder processes are worth MEI's time across our priority markets, and keep that view current as new market structures emerge
  • Lead viability assessments across every candidate market: document whether and when MEI can interconnect and earn capacity, on a timeline that supports capital allocation decisions
  • Represent MEI directly with ISOs, commissions, and utility program teams, building the relationships and credibility that get MEI a seat when programs and tariffs are designed
  • Co-design those programs and tariffs so storage and solar read as the utility's solution to capacity, reliability, and local benefit, not an obligation to accommodate
  • Build the bench — outside counsel, technical consultants, and AI tools — so the work doesn't run through one person
  • Translate regulatory reality into commercial terms for development, commercial, finance, and Digital Infrastructure Partnerships, and brief the CDO, Executive Team, and Board on how those assumptions are evolving

Qualifications

Required

  • Bachelor’s degree, with coursework or experience in engineering, economics, public policy, or a related field
  • 8+ years in utility regulatory strategy, grid or resource planning, DER program design, market design, or regulatory consulting, including meaningful time inside a utility, commission, or ISO/RTO, or advising them closely
  • A demonstrated track record of changing an outcome: a tariff, program, interconnection standard, or market rule that exists in its current form in part because of your work
  • Technical fluency in distributed storage and solar — interconnection, hosting capacity, aggregation, capacity accreditation — and a working understanding of how each flows through to project economics
  • Ability to write for a regulatory audience and to explain the same content to a commercial team in plain language
  • Self-directed operator comfortable representing MEI alone in a room of utility and commission counterparts, and holding a position respectfully when it matters
  • Willing and able to travel 30–40% for utility, commission, and ISO/RTO engagement

Preferred

  • PJM experience, including capacity market and accreditation mechanics, and familiarity with state distributed generation programs (Illinois, Maryland, Ohio, New York, Virginia)
  • Experience with FERC proceedings and formal ISO/RTO stakeholder processes
  • Familiarity with DER aggregation, DERMS, virtual power plants, and non-wires alternatives
  • Experience building new programs or functions inside a large, complex organization
  • Comfortable using artificial intelligence tools and capable of building agents to perform specific tasks

What We Value

  • Sound judgment about where to spend MEI's effort; knows which dockets, rules, and relationships move the 1 GW plan, and which don't
  • Credible alone in the room with utility and commission counterparts; holds a position under pressure without burning the relationship
  • Commercial lens on regulatory engagement; translates rule changes into what they mean for project economics and capital allocation
  • Intellectual rigor and honesty in technical assessment, especially when the answer is "this market doesn't pencil yet"
  • Collaborative across development, commercial, finance, and outside counsel without losing ownership of the call
  • Interest in utility and grid modernization

Benefits

  • PTO and company holidays
  • Medical, dental, vision
  • Employer-paid short-term disability, long-term disability, life insurance
  • 401(k) and company match
  • Professional development stipend
  • Strong culture of collaboration, performance, and personal growth
$150,000 - $200,000 a year
The actual salary offered may vary depending on job-related factors including, but not limited to knowledge, skills, experience and location.

How We Work

At Madison Energy Infrastructure, we believe in the power of clean energy infrastructure to drive real impact—for our customers, our partners, and the communities we serve. We’ve quickly emerged as a preeminent developer, investor, and operator of distributed generation, helping organizations across sectors meet their energy goals with certainty, speed, and trust. Our robust portfolio consists of over half a gigawatt of clean energy infrastructure projects across more than 25 states.
We’re building a team that thrives on ownership and ambition. As we expand into direct, end-to-end services for Fortune 500 companies, public entities, and nonprofits alike, we rely on collaborative thinkers who bring structure to complexity, energy to execution, and curiosity to every challenge.
Our environment is fast-paced and outcome-oriented—but grounded in the belief that how we work together matters as much as what we deliver. If you’re excited to shape the future of clean energy and be part of a high-performance, high-integrity team, we’d love to meet you.
Madison Energy Infrastructure is an equal opportunity employer. All applicants will be considered for employment without attention to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, veteran, or disability status.

jobs.description:
About Us

At Prenuvo, we are on a mission to flip the paradigm from reactive “sick-care” to proactive health care. Our award-winning whole body scan is fast (under 1 hour), safe (MRI has no ionizing radiation), and non-invasive (no contrast). Our unique integrated stack of optimized hardware, software, and increasingly AI, coupled with the patient-centric experience across our domestic and global clinics, have allowed us to lead the change against “we caught it too late again".

We are looking for a Staff Product Operations Specialist to build the connective tissue between the products we create and the teams who use, support, and deliver them. You will help Prenuvo turn product changes into successful organizational change. This role will own much of the operational machinery behind launches and rollouts: change-impact assessment, readiness, enablement, communications, adoption measurement, feedback loops, and continuous improvement.

You will work particularly closely with the teams responsible for delivering the patient experience, including our clinical and Preventive Health teams, as our products increasingly shape how care is delivered. At the same time, Prenuvo is a scale-up. The boundaries of this job will not always be neat. You will also help improve product processes, Voice of Customer systems, pilots, launch coordination, and the operating rhythms that allow Product teams to work effectively.

This role does not provide visa sponsorship. Applicants must be legally authorized to work in the United States at the time of hire and must not require employer sponsorship for a work visa (current or future).

Help reshape the world through proactive healthcare while working with cutting-edge technology and high performing teams with deep expertise - join us to make a difference in people’s lives!

What You'll Do

  • Create a scalable approach for preparing the organization for new products, workflows, capabilities, and process changes.
  • Conduct change-impact assessments across teams, workflows, policies, tools, training, and the patient experience.
  • Build rollout and adoption plans with Product, Clinical, Operations, Marketing, Support, and other stakeholders.
  • Translate product and technical changes into clear guidance, training, documentation, communications, and readiness activities.
  • Partner with Product Managers and TPMs to embed operational readiness into launches and identify dependencies and adoption risks early.
  • Coordinate pilots, phased releases, Early Access Programs, and internal testing, with clear launch success criteria and adoption measures.
  • Monitor rollout performance, address post-launch friction, and turn real-world feedback into product and operational improvements.
  • Build mechanisms for collecting and synthesizing feedback from patients and internal users across clinical, operational, commercial, and support teams.
  • Translate feedback and operational signals into clear themes and actionable recommendations, distinguishing isolated requests from systemic problems.
  • Ensure frontline insights reach Product teams early enough to influence planning and product decisions.
  • Strengthen product-development processes, tooling, planning rituals, launch calendars, intake processes, decision frameworks, and roadmap visibility.
  • Coordinate stakeholder input into planning and prioritization, simplify Product processes, and support high-priority cross-functional initiatives without a natural organizational home.

What You’ll Bring

  • 8+ years of experience in Product Operations, Product Management, Program Management, Business Operations, Change Management, or a related field.
  • Experience building processes and programs from scratch in a fast-moving organization.
  • Demonstrated experience leading complex product launches or organizational rollouts.
  • Strong change-management instincts, including stakeholder analysis, communications, training, readiness, and adoption measurement.
  • Experience turning qualitative and quantitative feedback into actionable product recommendations.
  • Strong cross-functional leadership and the ability to influence without formal authority.
  • Excellent written communication and an ability to make complicated changes easy for others to understand.
  • Comfort moving between strategic problems and highly tactical execution.
  • Experience working with internal tools or workflows used by operational teams.
  • Healthcare or health-technology experience is preferred but not required.
  • Experience with AI-enabled products or complex technical products is a plus.
  • Experience in a high-growth or scale-up environment is strongly preferred.

Our Values

First: we are Pioneers

  • Transforming healthcare requires divergent thinking, bias for action, disciplined experimentation, and consistent grit and determination to maintain momentum. This journey is as challenging as it is rewarding.

Second: we are Platform-Builders

  • We’re always building foundations that allow us to achieve tomorrow more than we did today. We never lose sight of what’s ahead – in a mindset of ownership and duty to our mission.

Above all: we are Patients

  • We could all be the next person who walks through our very doors, seeking clarity or peace of mind. We are proud of our impact on our patients’ lives, and we won’t stop till everyone can benefit from our work.

What We Offer

  • An avenue to make a positive impact on people's lives and their health
  • We believe in preventative healthcare for everyone, including our team - Prenuvo provides free, whole-body scans to each team member
  • Growth opportunities are at the heart of our people journey, we’re doing big things with bright minds - there is no single path to success, it can be shaped along the way
  • Building strong relationships is at the core of everything we do - our team gets together each week to connect, share, and socialize
  • Recognizing time away to restore is vital to our wellbeing - we have a flexible vacation policy and we will encourage you to use it
  • Prenuvo offers a 401(k) retirement savings plan to eligible employees, allowing team members to make pre-tax contributions toward their retirement. While Prenuvo facilitates access to the plan, the company does not currently offer matching contributions.
  • We offer a comprehensive benefits package including health, dental, vision, including Mental Health coverage, to support you and your family
  • The base salary for this role ranges from $170,000-$196,000 in local currency, depending upon experience and geographic location

jobs.title: Director, Social
jobs.excerpt: ABOUT OLIPOPAt OLIPOP, we’re on a mission to positively impact consumer health at scale.
jobs.description:
ABOUT OLIPOP

At OLIPOP, we’re on a mission to positively impact consumer health at scale. And we’re doing it through something simple: soda. But not just any soda, a new kind of soda: one that’s delicious, refreshing, and actually good for you.

This mission is deeply personal for our CEO, Co-Founder, and Formulator, Ben Goodwin. Like many of us, Ben grew up consuming the Standard American Diet: lots of soda and processed foods that prioritized convenience over nutrition. But at 14, he took his health into his own hands. After making significant changes to his nutrition and exercise, he lost 50 pounds and saw a transformation in his energy, mood, and emotional clarity.

Those changes sparked a deep curiosity about the connection between nutrition and health. Ben became a relentless student of the gut microbiome and the ways it supports overall wellness. The more he discovered, the more passionate he became about finding credible, science-backed ways to make consumer health accessible to everyone.

The mission was clear. The vehicle? Less so. After exploring the possibilities, Ben landed on an unexpected yet familiar choice: soda. It was something he loved as a kid, and he knew millions shared that same nostalgia. But this wouldn’t be just any soda. With most Americans falling short on daily fiber, Ben set out to create a version with more fiber and less sugar, one that was perfectly balanced. The result? A deliciously refreshing soda with 6 to 9 grams of fiber and 2 to 5 grams of sugar, delivering science-backed benefits without sacrificing the classic taste people crave.

In 2018, the first OLIPOP cans hit the shelves, bringing Ben’s vision to life with a functional soda that anyone could enjoy. And by reimagining soda, we’re also reshaping culture. That means creating products that support health for all and building a business grounded in humanistic values: empathy, integrity, and a belief in better for everyone. From the ingredients we source to the culture we foster, we’re committed to proving that business (and beverage!) can be a force for good, and that soda has the power to bring people together.

So join us, and let’s write a new American soda story together. One we can all feel good about. One OLIPOP at a time.

THE ROLE

The Director of Social Media will lead OLIPOP’s social presence and shape how the brand shows up in culture every day. Reporting to the Sr. Director, PR + Comms, this role sits at the intersection of strategy, creativity, culture, and communications, with responsibility for building a social-first approach that strengthens the brand, drives meaningful engagement, and supports broader business and marketing goals. This is a highly strategic and creative role for a social leader who understands that great social is more than content—it is about having a distinct point of view, creating ideas people want to talk about, and knowing how to make a brand matter in culture. The Director will set the vision and strategy across OLIPOP’s social channels, while also pushing the team and partners to create work that is innovative, culturally relevant, and unmistakably OLIPOP.

The Director will partner closely with Brand, Creative, Influencer, PR, Partnerships, and other Marketing teams to develop integrated campaigns and social-first ideas. They will identify opportunities for OLIPOP to participate in cultural moments, emerging conversations, trends, and communities, while also creating original opportunities for the brand to lead the conversation. The Director will lead and mentor OLIPOP’s growing social team, establishing clear ways of working, developing talent, and creating an environment where strategic thinking and creative ideas can thrive. They will also serve as a senior voice on social culture, providing perspective on emerging trends, audience behavior, cultural shifts, and potential risks.

Ultimately, this person will be responsible for making OLIPOP’s social presence strategic, culturally connected, creatively ambitious, and consistently true to the brand.

RESPONSIBILITIES

Social Strategy

  • Develop and own OLIPOP’s overarching social media strategy and vision across Instagram, TikTok, Meta, LinkedIn, and emerging platforms.
  • Establish channel-specific strategies that ladder back to OLIPOP’s brand platform, communications priorities, and broader Marketing KPIs.
  • Define how OLIPOP should show up in culture and identify opportunities to build relevance beyond traditional brand moments.
  • Translate business and brand objectives into clear, compelling social strategies and creative briefs.
  • Establish a strong point of view on what makes OLIPOP distinctive in social and continuously evolve the brand’s approach.

Creative & Innovation

  • Lead the development of social-first creative ideas and campaigns that are culturally relevant, innovative, and built for how people actually use and experience social platforms.
  • Partner closely with Creative leadership to develop and execute work that pushes the brand forward while remaining rooted in OLIPOP’s identity.
  • Bring new ideas, formats, platforms, partnerships, and creative approaches to the table rather than simply responding to existing trends.
  • Identify emerging cultural moments, internet behaviors, communities, creators, and trends that can create meaningful opportunities for OLIPOP.
  • Push the team and agency/production partners to continually raise the creative bar across social content.
  • Oversee social creative development from brief through execution, ensuring work is strategically grounded and creatively strong.

Content & Channel Management

  • Oversee the development of social content calendars and channel plans.
  • Ensure content is tailored to the unique role, audience, and behavior of each platform.
  • Partner with Producers and Creative teams to establish efficient production calendars, processes, and workflows.
  • Ensure the social team is set up to move quickly and capitalize on timely cultural and platform opportunities.
  • Balance planned brand storytelling with the flexibility to respond to real-time moments and conversations.

Cross-Functional Collaboration

  • Partner closely with Brand, Creative, Influencer, PR, Partnerships, and other Marketing teams to develop integrated campaigns and ensure social is considered from the start of major initiatives.
  • Collaborate with Influencer and Partnerships teams to strategically integrate creators, partners, and cultural voices into OLIPOP’s social ecosystem.
  • Build strong relationships across the organization and advocate for social as a critical part of how OLIPOP builds its brand.

Culture, Community & Risk

  • Maintain a deep, up-to-the-moment understanding of social platforms, internet culture, communities, and emerging behaviors.
  • Understand both macro and micro cultural shifts and translate those insights into actionable opportunities for OLIPOP.
  • Develop a strong understanding of OLIPOP’s audiences and the communities where the brand can authentically participate.
  • Monitor cultural and social risks and provide thoughtful guidance on potential issues, trends, conversations, and brand responses.
  • Partner with PR + Comms and relevant stakeholders on social crisis and issues management when needed.

Measurement & Optimization

  • Establish clear social KPIs and measurement frameworks aligned with broader Marketing and business objectives.
  • Analyze performance and audience insights to understand what is working, what is not, and where to evolve.
  • Turn data and insights into actionable strategic and creative recommendations.
  • Regularly communicate social performance, learnings, opportunities, and recommendations to senior leadership.
  • Balance quantitative performance with qualitative measures of cultural relevance, brand engagement, and creative impact.

QUALIFICATIONS

  • 10+ years of experience in social media, brand marketing, communications, or a related discipline, with significant experience leading social strategy.
  • 5+ years of experience leading and developing a team of social, community managers, and content creators, setting clear goals and fostering a collaborative culture that drives on-brand content and audience engagement
  • Demonstrated ability to develop strategic, creative, and innovative social programs that build brands and drive meaningful engagement.
  • Strong creative instincts and the ability to identify a great idea, develop a point of view, and translate strategy into compelling creative.
  • Deep, up-to-the-moment understanding of major social platforms, including platform behaviors, best practices, algorithms, formats, policies, and emerging trends.
  • Deep understanding of internet and social culture, including the ability to identify meaningful shifts before they become mainstream.
  • Strong understanding of audience behavior and the ability to translate cultural and consumer insights into social strategy and creative opportunities.
  • Ability to balance long-term strategic thinking with the speed and flexibility required of social.
  • Strong analytical skills and the ability to turn data and insights into clear strategic and creative recommendations.
  • Excellent cross-functional collaboration and communication skills, with the ability to influence senior stakeholders and creative partners.
  • CPG experience required.
  • Experience working at an advertising, creative, PR, or social agency preferred but not required.
  • Experience managing external agencies, creators, production partners, or other external social resources preferred.

REPORTS TO:

Sr. Director, PR + Comms

COMPENSATION:

$165,000 - $175,000 + Bonus

HOW WE WORK

We may be fully remote, but we’re anything but disconnected. OLIPOP has grown from a few passionate people around a table to a nationwide team, and we’ve done it without losing our collaborative spirit or sense of purpose.

Connection here is intentional. From cross-functional projects and IRL offsites to thoughtful Slack threads and spontaneous gifs, we make the effort to stay close, even across time zones. Sure, we move quickly, but we lead with trust, transparency, and a shared commitment to doing work that matters.

We value thoughtful debate. We give feedback with care and receive it with curiosity, knowing that real growth, both personal and collective, comes from listening as much as leading. Because at OLIPOP, it’s not just about getting things done. It’s about growing together, staying true to what matters, and building something with lasting impact.

WHAT WE VALUE

At OLIPOP, our values aren’t just posters on a wall. They shape how we show up: for each other, for our customers, and for the mission we’re chasing together.

  • Mission Connectivity: Everything we do ladders up to our shared goal: supporting human health. Whether launching a new flavor or conducting clinical research, the mission stays front and center.
  • Indomitable Spirit: When things get messy, we get inventive. We stay curious, adapt quickly, and find the path forward, most likely with a dedicated Slack thread and a beautifully overbuilt deck.
  • Lead at Every Level: Leadership isn’t about titles, it’s about ownership. We speak up, follow through, and lift each other up. If you’ve got ideas and initiative, you’ve got influence.
  • Courageous Humility: We’re confident in what we bring and curious about what we don’t know (yet). We give feedback with care, take it with grace, and know that real growth takes both.

WHAT WE’RE LOOKING FOR

Success at OLIPOP doesn’t come from checking boxes; it comes from living our values, staying curious, and finding energy in both the pace and the purpose. We’re building something big, and we’re looking for people who:

  • Think big, move fast, and take thoughtful risks
  • Thrive in a high-performance, feedback-rich environment
  • Value real human connection and honest collaboration
  • Are fired up by building something new, and making it better every day

Startup life at OLIPOP is equally fun and fast-paced. If you’re energized by a dynamic environment, eager to grow, and excited to help shape something meaningful from the inside out, OLIPOP is a one-of-a-kind ride.

Position Summary:  

As a founding engineer of the newly formed Innovation team, you will build and ship solutions with real complexity and scale to tens of thousands of clients. You will also play a key role in foundational decisions about architecture, design, systems, data, and product, wearing both Engineering and Product hats.


This is a rare opportunity to build product at the 0 to 1 stage, and ship it immediately to scale. You will work directly with Will Peng, Chief Innovation Officer — a former founder of a fintech company that raised $40M and exited in 2025.


About Cerity Partners

Cerity Partners is the one of the largest and fastest growing independent financial advisory firms, managing over $160+ billion in assets under management, and over $1 trillion assets under advisement. We serve high- and ultra-high-net-worth individuals and families, business owners, and institutions with comprehensive financial planning, investment, tax, and retirement solutions.


Backed by growth capital from Genstar Capital, Warburg Pincus, and Lightyear Capital, Cerity Partners ranks in the top 10 RIA's in the country by Barron's. Founded in 2009, we are extremely entrepreneurial and feel we are still in the early innings.


Our mission is to make every client steadier than we found them. We measure ourselves not by what we deliver, but by whether the people who trust us are better for it. Advice, service, and care do not bend to compensation, affiliation, or convenience — and they do not bend to the size of the client. We uphold the fiduciary standard at its highest levels.


The Innovation Team at Cerity Partners

Cerity Partners' Innovation Team is the firm's center of excellence for the strategy and deployment of technology and applied AI.


We are combining the best of technology and professional services to build the future of financial services. We believe the biggest opportunity is in the application of AI to scaled, complex industries like wealth and investment management — to raise the bar for quality of service, in service to our clients.


This is a rare opportunity to join a generational company at a key inflection point. We are extremely ambitious and entrepreneurial, and approach innovation with a "blank sheet of paper" mindset — so there will be no shortage of exciting technical challenges to work on.


We approach every problem through the lens of experience and design, with the client at the center. Our team partners with colleagues across the entire business to understand workflows, and create cohesive experiences across the client, advisor, and colleague journey.


Our vision is to build the new OS of wealth intelligence. We are building the entire AI stack — harness, context, memory, evals, agents, models, workflows, data, knowledge — both in applying it to wealth management, as well as in how we work and collaborate with each other.


By fully leveraging the insights and institutional expertise of the firm, we will move the firm into a client-first, AI-native era.


Primary Responsibilities:

  • Own the end-to-end experience: The Innovation Team is highly autonomous, and you will be responsible for full user journeys and business goals, not just a silo. You will build the solution or partner with the best vendor — whatever is the best for the need — and integrate them into a cohesive platform. You will have the opportunity to build both 0-to-1, as well as scale products post-launch.
  • Build in partnership with clients, advisors, and colleagues: Identify high value opportunities, understand their needs and root problems, map workflows, test prototypes and hypotheses, and build and advocate for the best experience.
  • Establish foundational engineering principles and product strategy: The decisions you make about engineering and product are the foundation of our platform, architecture, data, client experience, advisor experience, and colleague experience. These are decisions that can drive business strategy, goals, differentiation, and prioritization.
  • Build at the cutting edge of applied AI: Work across every part of the AI stack — harness, context, memory, evals, agents, models — both in applying it to wealth management, as well as in how we work and collaborate.

Required Qualifications: 

  • Years of experience: Minimum of 7 years
  • Financial services industry experience required - understanding of wealth management, investment advisory, or related financial services operations
  • Demonstrated experience in AI tooling, models, harnesses, workflows
  • Demonstrated ability to operate in ambiguity and building 0-to-1 products from first principles rather than established processes.
  • Expertise and experience with Claude Code, Codex, or similar

Skills and Competencies: 

  • You have a track record of outsized impact: Your impact extends beyond individual features. Your work has created broad, lasting results on the customer, your colleagues, and in the foundational systems that endure.
  • You are a systems thinker: You are able to see the bigger picture and the patterns that emerge. You are able to consider decisions in the broader context, and know what are the most important factors to consider
  • You have excellent product and business intuition: You know what decisions will have wide-ranging impact. You put experience and the user first. You know where to cut, and what is important.
  • You lead with agency: You take initiative and move work forward independently. You navigate obstacles resourcefully while building the trust, alignment, and influence needed to mobilize others and amplify your impact.
  • You move quickly with rigor: You have a bias towards action for learning. You balance speed and quality, demonstrating a high shipping velocity, rapid learning, and a hypothesis-driven approach.
  • You thrive in ambiguity: You are energized by new, undefined, ambiguous spaces, and excel in shaping the right approach as the space changes quickly. You are humble and adaptable. You have a demonstrated record of creating and shipping real products—not simply operating within established systems. As a founding engineer, you will help define the systems themselves.
  • You are passionate about AI: You have experience building and shipping AI agents and harnesses. You stay close to emerging capabilities, continually experimenting to identify where they create meaningful opportunity.
  • You do your best work when collaborating with others: You love working with cross-functional teams, connecting feedback, workflows, and downstream implications to make coherent decisions across the organization

Compensation Range:

$190,000 - $290,000 (salary & bonus)


Why Cerity Partners:

Our people drive our success by working together to deliver exceptional service to our clients. Below is a glimpse of the key elements of our total rewards package:

About You

You are an AI Developer who turns large language models into reliable, production-ready data logic. You will join the team building a migration platform, where an LLM proposes SQL and mappings, a person reviews and approves them, and the approved logic is reused at scale. Your focus will be the reverse direction of the sync, taking changes made in the target platform back into each source system, along with the rules that classify and resolve the records that fail to sync.

Note: This position is offered under a 6-month contractor framework, with the possibility of extension.

You Bring to Applaudo the Following Competencies:

  • Bachelor's Degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Information Systems, or a related field is desired, or equivalent professional experience.
  • 3+ years of software development experience with Python and software engineering best practices.
  • Advanced SQL skills working with PostgreSQL, MySQL, and cloud data warehouses such as BigQuery.
  • 1+ year of experience building LLM applications that run in production, beyond prototypes.
  • Experience integrating hosted LLM APIs into production environments, including structured output and its validation.
  • Experience with prompt engineering, prompt versioning, fallback strategies, and cost and latency optimization.
  • Experience evaluating LLM output with test cases and clear evaluation methodologies.
  • Demonstrated ability to understand and modify a partially documented codebase that you did not write.
  • Demonstrated use of AI tools in your daily workflow, with an explicit step to verify what they produce.
  • Strong autonomy, attention to detail, and comfort with ambiguity as requirements evolve.
  • Advanced English fluency.

Nice to haves:

  • Experience in data migration or ETL projects.
  • Experience with Vertex AI or Gemini.
  • Experience extracting data from spreadsheets or documents.
  • Experience with MLOps practices, including CI/CD, observability, and reproducible pipelines.

You Will Be Accountable for the Following Responsibilities:

  • Prepare the context for each migration process, including functional documentation, source schema, and target data model, so the LLM generates accurate mappings in both directions.
  • Design and tune the prompts the LLM uses to propose queries, mappings, and transformation rules, reducing rework during human review.
  • Review generated SQL and mappings against both data models, validating entities, fields, relationships, and constraints.
  • Resolve cases the LLM does not handle reliably, such as identifiers that change format between systems or data that conflicts with a constraint, while keeping the constraint in place.
  • Build parameterized queries that detect what changed on each side since the last sync, including sources that are not databases, such as spreadsheets and document folders.
  • Work with the Senior Python Developer on safeguards for LLM-generated SQL, enabling controlled and approved writes to source systems.
  • Automatically classify records that fail to sync by root cause, including conflicts where the same data changed on both sides, and turn each treatment into an approved rule.
  • Automate repetitive migration preparation tasks, such as loading inputs, generating artifacts, and comparing artifact versions.
  • Version every approved artifact together with the inputs that produced it, and document the preparation procedure so other teams can reuse it.
  • 3+ years of experience with Python, plus advanced SQL on PostgreSQL, MySQL, and BigQuery
  • Production LLM applications experience, including hosted LLM API integration, structured output, and validation
  • Prompt engineering and versioning, fallback strategies, cost and latency optimization, and LLM evaluation methodologies

About Us

We Are Engineered Different.

At Applaudo, talented people design, build, and scale meaningful, AI-powered solutions that create real business impact. As an AI-native organization, we collaborate across design, development, cloud, data, and artificial intelligence to turn ideas into scalable products that transform how companies operate, make decisions, and grow.

We are building a high-performance culture grounded in five values: Empowering Excellence, Collaborative Teamwork, Unsolicited Respect, Consistent Transparency, and Efficient Communication. These define how we work, how we support one another, and how we hold ourselves accountable.

Applaudo is a place for people who want to learn fast, take ownership, and work alongside strong teams they are proud to belong to. Joining us means being part of an organization that is evolving intentionally, investing in modern ways of working, and leading AI-native transformation at scale.

Description

Customer Success Manager (CSM) – Browzwear

Browzwear is a leading provider of 3D fashion design and simulation software, driving digital transformation in the fashion industry. The company has pioneered the use of 3D design for apparel and is widely adopted by major fashion brands and manufacturers.

As a Customer Success Manager at Browzwear, you’ll play a key role in delivering meaningful outcomes across the customer journey—from onboarding through renewal and expansion. You’ll join a growing global team focused on driving long-term value for our customers and enabling sustainable growth for the business.

You’ll partner closely with Sales, Product, and Support to ensure every customer receives exceptional service, sees real impact, and feels supported at every touchpoint. This role is ideal for someone who thrives in a high-performance environment, enjoys building trusted relationships, and is motivated by delivering results.

Position Summary

At Browzwear, we’re transforming the fashion industry with cutting-edge AI and digital twin technology. Our platform empowers the world’s leading brands and manufacturers to bring products to market faster, smarter, and more sustainably.

The Customer Success Manager (CSM) is responsible for ensuring Browzwear customers derive maximum value from their investment in our 3D fashion design software. The CSM will focus on driving customer adoption, engagement, retention, and expansion, ensuring that customers achieve their desired business outcomes across a portfolio of enterprise and mid-market accounts.

The ideal candidate has a strong understanding of Enterprise B2B High touch SaaS CSM role, with experience in the fashion or apparel industry, and excels in relationship management and problem-solving.

﻿Key Responsibilities

1. Customer Onboarding and Enablement

  • Ensure new customers have a seamless onboarding process.
  • Arrange training sessions to educate customers on software capabilities and best practices.

2. Account Management

  • Build and maintain strong relationships with key stakeholders, acting as the primary point of contact.
  • Develop and execute customer success plans tailored to each client’s business goals.
  • Regularly review account health, usage data, and feedback to identify growth and optimization opportunities.
  • Inspire customers with industry best practices and cross pollinate knowledge to encourage steady adoption & value realization

3. Adoption and Engagement

  • Partner with customer as a thought leader in driving business transformation, workflow optimization, and adoption of digital first workflows
  • Proactively identify & align software adoption & expansion to customer’s business outcomes and continuously measure delivery of business outcomes
  • Monitor customer usage and engagement metrics to ensure effective adoption of Browzwear solutions.
  • Proactively address barriers to adoption through targeted interventions.
  • Partner with customers to drive change management and digital transformation enablement, helping them integrate Browzwear solutions into core business processes

4. Renewals and Expansion

  • Collaborate with Sales and Account Management to secure renewals and identify upsell opportunities.
  • Present value-driven ROI cases to demonstrate the impact of Browzwear’s platform on the customer’s business outcomes.

5. Customer Advocacy

  • Serve as the voice of the customer within Browzwear by providing feedback to Product, Engineering, and Customer Success teams.
  • Advocate for customer needs in shaping product roadmap priorities.

6. Issue Resolution and Support Coordination

  • Resolve customer issues promptly.
  • Coordinate cross-functional resources to address complex customer challenges.

KPIs for Success

  • Customer retention (GRR) and Net Revenue Retention (NRR).
  • Time to Value (TTV) for new customer implementations.
  • Product adoption and feature utilization rates.
  • Customer satisfaction and Net Promoter Score (NPS).
  • Expansion revenue through upsells and cross-sells.

This position aligns closely with Browzwear’s goal of empowering customers to innovate faster, collaborate seamlessly, and achieve sustainable growth in the fashion industry.

Requirements

  • Bachelor’s degree in Business, Fashion Design, Engineering, or a related field; Master’s preferred.
  • 5+ years in Customer Success, Account Management, or a related role in SaaS or engagement management in top tier consulting firm
  • Demonstrated ability to drive customer retention by proactively managing account health, adoption, and satisfaction to support successful renewals and expansions
  • Ability to translate technology into business value and ROI-driven narratives.
  • Experience in the fashion or apparel industry is highly desirable.
  • Excellent interpersonal, communication, and negotiation skills.
  • Analytical mindset with the ability to interpret data and drive action.
  • Proficient in using CRM tools, analytics platforms, and Browzwear’s suite of products (preferred).
  • Comfort working across global, cross-functional teams in a fast-paced environment.
  • Fluency in spoken & written English is mandatory & additional languages are welcome
