jobs.excerpt: Career CategoryGovernment AffairsJob DescriptionJoin Amgen’s Mission of Serving Patients At Amgen, if you feel like you’re part of something bigger, it’s because you are.
jobs.description:
Career Category

Government Affairs

Job Description

Join Amgen’s Mission of Serving Patients


At Amgen, if you feel like you’re part of something bigger, it’s because you are. Our shared mission—to serve patients living with serious illnesses—drives all that we do.


Since 1980, we’ve helped pioneer the world of biotech in our fight against the world’s toughest diseases. With our focus on four therapeutic areas –Oncology, Inflammation, General Medicine, and Rare Disease– we reach millions of patients each year. Amgen is advancing a broad and deep pipeline of medicines to treat cancer, heart disease, inflammatory conditions, rare diseases, and obesity and obesity-related conditions. As a member of the Amgen team, you’ll help make a lasting impact on the lives of patients as we research, manufacture, and deliver innovative medicines to help people live longer, fuller happier lives.


Our award-winning culture is collaborative, innovative, and science based. If you have a passion for challenges and the opportunities that lay within them, you’ll thrive as part of the Amgen team. Join us and transform the lives of patients while transforming your career.


Senior Director, Consumer Pricing & Non-Reimbursed Channels, Obesity and Related Conditions (OaR)


Amgen has an exciting opportunity for an individual looking to make a significant impact on the Obesity and Related Conditions launch of MariTide. As a member of the Obesity Value & Access leadership team, the Sr Director, Consumer Pricing & Non-Reimbursed Channels, Obesity and Related Conditions will be integral to the launch's consumer access, net sales and long-term value performance. The Sr Director will lead U.S. consumer pricing and non-reimbursed channel strategy and performance activities for MariTide, and the broader OaR strategy for future indications and assets.


The leader will translate MariTide's value proposition and consumer and market insights into clear, consumer-centered cash-price and channel strategies; establish the governance and operating model required to make high-quality pricing decisions; and lead the consumer pricing market research needed to inform launch and lifecycle pricing decisions.

The Senior Director, Consumer Pricing & Non-Reimbursed Channels, Obesity and Related Conditions is responsible for the end-to-end U.S. consumer/cash pricing and non-reimbursed channel agenda supporting the MariTide obesity launch. They will lead consumer pricing strategy, consumer pricing market research and insights, cash-channel insights, offer and discount strategy, channel economics, partner-negotiation frameworks, governance and launch readiness to establish and improve sustainable patient access. This includes shaping the consumer pricing research and translating those insights into actionable pricing and channel recommendations.


The role will coordinate consumer/cash-channel needs across direct-to-patient, retail, telehealth/provider, pharmacy and distribution partners. The role will collaborate as needed with other leaders driving payer/PBM coverage, copay design, government pricing and employer strategy. While this role will focus primarily on US there may be requirements to shape elements of the Outside US framework.


Key responsibilities also include:


  • Lead MariTide consumer cash pricing strategy and execution across direct-to-patient, retail cash, telehealth provider, pharmacy and other non-reimbursed routes; recommend price architecture, guardrails and lifecycle actions that optimize access, demand, persistence and net sales.
  • Own consumer and cash-channel insight synthesis, including willingness-to-pay, price elasticity, competitor offers, affordability, fulfillment, persistence, channel economics and emerging behaviors; translate insights into executive recommendations.
  • Establish and lead consumer pricing governance, including a consumer price committee or equivalent forum, decision rights, escalation pathways, review cadence, scenario analyses and documentation for timely, compliant decisions.
  • Own launch and lifecycle consumer price, discount and offer strategy, including start-price recommendations, introductory and retention offers, channel-specific pricing principles and patient-segmentation guardrails; monitor performance and recommend adjustments.
  • Develop the negotiation framework for cash-channel partners, including commercial objectives, pricing and discount guardrails, economics, contractual principles, performance measures and renewal strategy; lead strategic negotiations as appropriate.
  • Define and manage the non-reimbursed channel gross-to-net and financial framework with Finance, Forecasting, Pricing & Contracting and Trade; quantify cash price, discounts, fees, service costs, product flow and channel economics to inform forecasts and decisions.
  • Partner with PAR, direct-to-patient, Trade, Operations and digital teams to translate approved strategies into platform, pharmacy/distribution, product-data, consumer-communications, measurement and issue-resolution requirements. Implementation ownership resides with the respective operational teams.
  • Present and translate recommendations, strategic options for the consumer-centered cash-price and channel strategies, and decision-enablement materials for senior leadership and governance forums, enabling efficient, data-driven decisions.
  • Lead the consumer pricing market research and insights for MariTide, establishing the strategic learning priorities required to inform launch and lifecycle consumer pricing, affordability, offer and non-reimbursed channel decisions.
  • Define an integrated consumer pricing research program and advanced pricing research approaches and analytical frameworks to understand consumer response across price points, offers, channels and segments, translating findings into implications for pricing architecture, demand, access, persistence, net sales and long-term price integrity.
  • Define the consumer pricing learning agenda before and after launch, research priorities and decision triggers to enable rapid learning and evidence-based evolution of pricing, discount and offer strategies.

What we expect of you


We are all different, yet we all use our unique contributions to serve patients. The professional we seek is a leader with these qualifications.


Basic Qualifications:


  • Doctorate degree & 5 years of commercial experience OR
  • Master’s degree & 8 years of commercial experience OR
  • Bachelor’s degree & 10 years of commercial experience

Preferred Qualifications:


  • Experience solving complex business problems in consumer-oriented, high-growth healthcare markets.
  • Advanced knowledge of U.S. pharmaceutical consumer and HCP marketing and insight development
  • Translatable experience in retail and cash-based pricing models, cash-pay or direct-to-patient models, channel economics and pricing/discount governance
  • Experience in obesity, consumer health, retail healthcare or a similarly complex category preferred.
  • Experience developing consumer pricing architecture, launch offers and price-promotion strategies that balance patient affordability, demand, channel economics, net sales and long-term price integrity.
  • Experience leading pricing decisions and negotiations and ability to adapt to novel entities in the cash channel.
  • Strong executive presence with experience supporting senior governance and decision-making forums
  • Demonstrated ability to influence without authority and drive alignment across diverse, global stakeholders
  • Strong quantitative capability with ability to communicate financial tradeoffs and performance measurement across price, discounts, fees and fulfillment.
  • Experience designing decision governance and presenting concise, data-driven recommendations and tradeoffs for executive decision making; strong executive communication skill.
  • Demonstrated track record of increasing responsibility and management of multiple, concurrent workstreams in a matrixed launch environment.
  • Strong orientation to teamwork; able to turn consumer and channel insights into executable strategies with Brand, PAR, direct-to-patient, Trade, Operations, Finance, Legal, Compliance and Analytics.
  • Remote work available with 25–30% travel depending on obesity brand, U.S. Value & Access and organizational needs.

What you can expect of us


As we work to develop treatments that take care of others, we also work to care for your professional and personal growth and well-being. From our competitive benefits to our collaborative culture, we’ll support your journey every step of the way.

jobs.description:
Senior Site Reliability Engineer

Remote | Australia

About Climavision  

At Climavision, we’re rebuilding climate technology from the ground up and changing the way we see weather. We merge the power of our proprietary, high-resolution weather radar and satellite network with advanced weather prediction modelling and decades of industry expertise to reduce existing coverage gaps and drastically improve forecasting ability. Our revolutionary new approach to climate technology weather solutions is poised to help reduce the economic risks of climate change on companies, governments, and societies alike. We are backed by The Rise Fund, the world’s largest global impact platform committed to achieving measurable, positive social and environmental outcomes alongside competitive financial returns. Climavision is headquartered in Louisville, KY, with research and development operations in Raleigh, NC.   

The Work

Are you an experienced Site Reliability Engineer who thrives at the intersection of software engineering and production operations? Do you take pride in keeping mission-critical customer systems reliable under real-world operational pressure? Are you looking for an opportunity to own production reliability for a modern hybrid infrastructure platform spanning cloud, colocation, and edge environments?

If so, we have an exceptional opportunity for you.

Climavision is seeking a Senior Site Reliability Engineer to contribute towards reliability, operational excellence, and production resilience across the company's platform and data services. This role sits on a shared SRE team that supports the full business rather than a single product line, covering both the radar network and the weather intelligence sides of the company as priorities shift. A central focus of this role is building the observability layer that puts the health of the full fleet in one place, and then automating recovery so that systems heal themselves. Multi-cluster and multi-replica high availability across our distributed edge fleet remains a core part of the work.

This is a hands-on engineering role for someone who is equally comfortable troubleshooting Kubernetes clusters, leading incident response, and improving operational maturity across the organization. The successful candidate will combine deep production operations expertise with a disciplined approach to reliability engineering and strong automation skills.

Climavision operates a hybrid infrastructure footprint spanning Microsoft Azure, colocation data centers, and edge Kubernetes clusters, deployed alongside weather radar systems. This role will drive production reliability across Azure, colocation, and edge environments. Right-sizing cluster resources and migrating workloads off Azure to reduce spend are active priorities for the team.

35% Kubernetes Platform Reliability and Operations

30% Production Reliability Engineering and Incident Response

20% Observability, Monitoring, and Alerting

15% Automation, Recovery, and Cost Optimization

Primary Responsibilities:

  • Own production reliability for Climavision's customer-facing platform and data services across Azure, colocation, and edge Kubernetes environments.
  • Work as part of a shared SRE function supporting the whole company rather than a single product line, taking on work across both the radar network and the weather intelligence sides of the business as priorities shift.
  • Contribute to the definition and improvement of SLIs, SLOs, alerting standards, and operational metrics used to measure platform reliability.
  • Build and own the observability layer for the fleet. Today the underlying metrics exist but are only reachable from the command line inside each cluster. This role is responsible for surfacing that data in shared dashboards and building the alerting that tells the team something is going wrong before a customer does.
  • Design and build automated recovery and self-healing for production systems, so that common failure modes are detected and remediated without human intervention.
  • Optimize cluster resourcing and cost, including right-sizing workloads and nodes and supporting the migration of workloads off Azure to reduce spend.
  • Support and coordinate production incident response efforts, including troubleshooting, mitigation, communication, and postmortem analysis.
  • Diagnose and resolve complex production issues across application services, Kubernetes infrastructure, storage, and distributed systems.
  • Drive multi-replica and multi-cluster high availability across Climavision's services, including workload placement, scheduling, and deployment patterns that allow services to run safely as multiple replicas across multiple clusters.
  • Contribute to the multi-cluster high-availability strategy across Climavision's hybrid fleet, including active-active and active-passive failover behavior, traffic routing, data replication considerations, and graceful degradation when a cluster becomes unavailable.
  • Operate and improve Climavision's self-managed Kubernetes platform spanning cloud-hosted, colocation, and edge clusters, with a focus on availability, resiliency, recovery, and operational performance.
  • Ensure Kubernetes platform lifecycle activities including upgrades, patching, cluster health, node management, and production change management are executed in a manner that preserves service availability and minimizes customer-facing risk.
  • Improve reliability and operational maturity of production platform services, including observability, autoscaling, ingress, and distributed storage. Partner with the teams responsible for the underlying networking and security primitives rather than owning those areas directly.
  • Design and validate Kubernetes workloads for resiliency, scalability, and operational efficiency, including autoscaling behavior, workload placement, resource management, and graceful degradation strategies.
  • Partner with software engineering teams across the company to improve production readiness, resiliency patterns, deployment safety, and operational visibility before services reach production.
  • Maintain and improve deployment pipelines, Helm charts, Kubernetes manifests, and infrastructure automation supporting safe and repeatable production releases.
  • Support and evolve Climavision's observability platform, including metrics, logging, distributed tracing, dashboarding, and alerting.
  • Conduct performance engineering and capacity-planning efforts for customer-facing services during peak weather-event demand.
  • Help facilitate blameless postmortem reviews and drive operational follow-up items through completion.
  • Improve disaster recovery, failover, and business continuity capabilities across cloud, colocation, and edge environments.
  • Drive operational excellence initiatives, including automation, reduction of operational toil, game days, production readiness reviews, and reliability best practices.
  • Contribute as a senior technical resource and mentor on reliability engineering and production operations practices.

On-Call Expectation:

Climavision operates customer-facing production systems under contractual SLAs that do not pause outside business hours. The Senior Site Reliability Engineer will participate in a rotating on-call schedule made up of two separate rotations:

  • A weekday rotation. The engineer on a weekday shift is the first point of contact for production incidents and for engineering teams needing support during the business week.
  • A separate weekend rotation, so that the engineer carrying weekday support is not also carrying the weekend.

At current and planned team size, engineers can expect a weekday shift roughly every five weeks and a weekend shift roughly every five weeks. The two are scheduled as far apart from each other as the rotation allows, so that a weekday shift and a weekend shift do not fall close together.

Qualifications

  • A bachelor's degree in computer science, software engineering, or a related field; equivalent professional experience considered.
  • Minimum of 7 years of experience in Site Reliability Engineering, DevOps, Production Engineering, Platform Engineering, or a related infrastructure-focused role, with at least 4 years in a role formally titled Site Reliability Engineer or carrying explicit SLO / error-budget accountability.
  • Deep, hands-on experience operating native Kubernetes. Managed distributions such as AKS and EKS are acceptable, but experience running native or self-managed Kubernetes is strongly preferred and is the primary technical requirement for this role.
  • Demonstrated experience optimizing Kubernetes clusters, including right-sizing workloads and node pools, resource management, and reducing infrastructure cost without sacrificing reliability. Be prepared to walk through a specific cluster optimization project you led.
  • Demonstrated experience increasing operational visibility, including building dashboards, metrics pipelines, and alerting in an environment where little or none existed before.
  • Experience designing and operating workloads for safe horizontal scaling across multiple replicas, including idempotency, concurrency, and state handling considerations.
  • Experience designing or operating multi-cluster high-availability architectures, including failover behavior, traffic routing, and cross-cluster service deployment.
  • Experience supporting customer-facing production systems with uptime, reliability, and incident-response responsibilities.
  • Experience diagnosing and resolving production incidents across application, platform and Kubernetes infrastructure layers, including workload scheduling, storage, ingress, and cluster-level failures.
  • Experience operating Kubernetes outside of strictly managed cloud environments, including bare-metal, colocation, edge, or hybrid infrastructure.
  • Experience with Kubernetes operational tooling and ecosystem technologies such as Rancher, Helm, autoscaling frameworks, observability stacks, or distributed storage systems.
  • Strong understanding of infrastructure automation and Infrastructure as Code concepts using tools such as Terraform and Ansible.
  • Experience supporting CI/CD and production deployment pipelines. GitHub Actions is used for CI/CD at Climavision.
  • Experience with monitoring, logging, and observability platforms such as DataDog, Prometheus, Grafana, Loki, OpenTelemetry, or comparable technologies.
  • Experience operating distributed systems and microservice-based architectures in production environments.
  • Working knowledge of Microsoft Azure infrastructure.
  • Strong troubleshooting skills across infrastructure, application, and platform layers.
  • Demonstrated experience participating in a structured production on-call rotation supporting business-critical systems.
  • Working familiarity with Jira, Confluence, and Microsoft Entra, which the team uses day to day for ticketing, documentation, and authentication.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, including incident documentation and postmortem authoring.
  • Experience working in start-up, scale-up, or other fast-moving engineering environments, and comfort with the pace and ambiguity that comes with them.

Nice to have, but not required:

  • Experience operating Kubernetes platforms using RKE2 and Rancher, which is how Climavision manages its clusters.

•Experience with Octopus Deploy.

  • Experience with SOC 2 or comparable security auditing and compliance work.
  • Experience supporting hybrid cloud and colocation infrastructure environments.
  • Experience with service mesh technologies such as Istio.
  • Experience with Kubernetes-native storage platforms such as Longhorn.
  • Experience operating PostgreSQL or PostGIS in Kubernetes environments.
  • Experience with distributed messaging systems such as RabbitMQ or NATS.
  • Experience supporting GPU-enabled workloads in Kubernetes.
  • Familiarity with reliability engineering practices, including SLIs, SLOs, error budgets, and operational maturity metrics.

Physical Demands & Work Environment:  

•This is a full-time, exempt position

•Fully Remote - Australia  

  • Candidates based in Australia should expect standard local business hours on the east coast of Australia, which provides overlap with the United States team in the early morning Eastern time.  
  • This job requires frequent use of a computer to complete tasks, attend meetings, and communicate via Microsoft Teams. 

Once you land this position, you’ll get to enjoy:  

  • Benefits of a dynamic and growing organization  
  • A challenging, hands-on role that will have real impact on the business  

•Competitive compensation 

•Comprehensive benefits package

•401(k) Savings Plan

  • Health Savings Account (HSA) and Flexible Spending Account (FSA)

•11 Paid Holidays

  • Company Paid Long-term Disability (LTD)

The salary range for this position is $130,000-170,000 annually, however Climavision considers several factors when extending an offer of employment including but not limited to, the applicant’s education, experience, the responsibilities of the role, training, knowledge, skills, and abilities, as well as internal equity and alignment with market data. Any offer of employment is contingent on completion of a background check to company standard. Please note this job description is not designed to cover or contain a comprehensive listing of activities, duties or responsibilities that are required of the employee for this job. jobs.title: Científico/a de Datos Espaciales y MEL (Monitoreo, Evaluación y Aprendizaje)
jobs.excerpt: Ubicación:Preferentemente Bogotá; sin embargo, se considerarán candidatos ubicados en cualquier ciudad principal de Colombia.
jobs.description:
Ubicación:Preferentemente Bogotá; sin embargo, se considerarán candidatos ubicados en cualquier ciudad principal de Colombia.

Tipo de contrato: Contrato a plazo fijo por 1 año.


Lo que podemos lograr juntos:

El/la Especialista en MEL contribuye al diseño, implementación y fortalecimiento de sistemas de Monitoreo, Evaluación y Aprendizaje (MEL) para Soluciones Basadas en la Naturaleza (SbN) y otras estrategias de conservación de TNC Colombia. Integra análisis y modelamiento espacial con información biofísica, climática, social y económica para generar evidencia que apoye la toma de decisiones, el aprendizaje y la gestión adaptativa.


Te estamos buscando:

Buscamos un/a profesional con experiencia en MEL y análisis espacial aplicado a la conservación, capaz de coordinar procesos técnicos, integrar y analizar datos, desarrollar indicadores y herramientas de seguimiento, y comunicar evidencia para apoyar decisiones de proyectos y portafolios. La persona trabajará de manera colaborativa con equipos interdisciplinarios, socios y comunidades, y reportará al Especialista en Ciencias y Adaptación de TNC Colombia.


RESPONSABILIDADES Y ALCANCE

· Coordinar el diseño, la implementación y la mejora continua de sistemas MEL para proyectos y portafolios de SbN, articulando teorías de cambio, preguntas de aprendizaje, marcos de resultados, planes de monitoreo, líneas base, metas, criterios de éxito y mecanismos de retroalimentación para la gestión adaptativa.

· Diseñar, validar y estandarizar indicadores de gestión, producto, resultado e impacto, combinando dimensiones biofísicas, climáticas, sociales, económicas y de gobernanza; establecer fichas técnicas, métodos de cálculo, fuentes, periodicidad, desagregaciones, responsabilidades y criterios de calidad.

· Diseñar y apoyar evaluaciones de pertinencia, coherencia, efectividad, eficiencia, impacto y sostenibilidad de las SbN, utilizando enfoques cuantitativos, cualitativos o mixtos acordes con las preguntas de evaluación, la disponibilidad de datos y el contexto de implementación.

· Asegurar que el monitoreo permita verificar las cadenas causales de las teorías de cambio, analizar supuestos y riesgos, diferenciar productos de resultados e impactos, y documentar resultados previstos y no previstos.

· Coordinar el diseño de protocolos de línea base, seguimiento y evaluación, y apoyar el levantamiento, la validación y el análisis de información de campo, sensores remotos y fuentes secundarias, asegurando rigor metodológico, representatividad, ética, trazabilidad y confiabilidad.

· Diseñar procesos participativos de monitoreo y aprendizaje con comunidades, pueblos indígenas, comunidades locales, socios y actores institucionales, integrando conocimiento científico y local y asegurando mecanismos apropiados de retroalimentación y validación.

· Gestionar y estandarizar la arquitectura y gobernanza de los datos de MEL, asegurando integridad, interoperabilidad, documentación, control de calidad, seguridad, reproducibilidad y principios FAIR, así como su integración con otros equipos y sistemas de TNC.

· Coordinar análisis y modelamiento espacial de GEI, biodiversidad, integridad y representatividad ecosistémica, riesgo climático, cambio de uso del suelo y áreas potenciales para SbN, vinculando los resultados con indicadores, líneas base, metas y evaluaciones de efectividad.

· Desarrollar y validar modelos predictivos, análisis multicriterio y métodos de teledetección y aprendizaje automático aplicados al monitoreo de cambios, la detección de tendencias y la evaluación de escenarios, documentando supuestos, limitaciones e incertidumbre.

· Diseñar herramientas de consulta, visualización y tableros de control que permitan dar seguimiento a avances, resultados, riesgos, supuestos y brechas de información, facilitando decisiones oportunas basadas en evidencia.

· Sintetizar hallazgos de monitoreo y evaluación en reportes técnicos, productos de aprendizaje y publicaciones científicas, y facilitar espacios de reflexión y uso de evidencia para ajustar estrategias, fortalecer prácticas y comunicar resultados a audiencias técnicas, institucionales y comunitarias.

· Brindar apoyo técnico especializado en MEL, ciencia de datos, mitigación, adaptación y biodiversidad; contribuir al aseguramiento de la calidad de términos de referencia, productos de consultoría y entregables científicos; y apoyar el fortalecimiento de capacidades de equipos interdisciplinarios.


Cualificaciones Mínimas

  • Maestría en ciencias ambientales, ciencias sociales, estadística, ciencia de datos, geografía, economía, ingeniería, medio ambiente o un campo científico relacionado, y al menos 1 año de experiencia relacionada, o combinación equivalente de educación y experiencia.
  • Experiencia en el diseño o la implementación de sistemas MEL, incluidos teorías de cambio, marcos de resultados, indicadores, líneas base, planes de monitoreo o procesos de aprendizaje y gestión adaptativa.
  • Experiencia aplicando métodos cuantitativos, cualitativos o mixtos para el monitoreo o la evaluación de resultados en proyectos de conservación, desarrollo sostenible o cambio climático.
  • Experiencia integrando y analizando datos espaciales, biofísicos, climáticos, sociales o económicos para elaborar productos técnicos o recomendaciones de gestión.
  • Experiencia en producción de mapas, análisis y modelamiento espacial, teledetección y procesamiento de datos de sensores remotos, incluidas imágenes satelitales, mediante herramientas como R, Python, Google Earth Engine, ArcGIS Pro o QGIS; y experiencia en gestión de bases de datos, automatización, control de calidad o reproducibilidad.
  • Experiencia en el diseño o implementación de encuestas, grupos focales, talleres o procesos participativos de monitoreo, incluida la documentación de métodos, el control de calidad, la trazabilidad o el uso ético de la información.

Cualificaciones Deseadas

  • Experiencia adicional coordinando componentes técnicos de MEL, evaluación, análisis espacial o ciencia aplicada en proyectos o portafolios de conservación y cambio climático.
  • Experiencia demostrada en monitoreo y evaluación de SbN, biodiversidad, mitigación, adaptación o resiliencia climática, incluidos indicadores sociales, económicos, biofísicos y de gobernanza.
  • Experiencia en gobernanza de datos, estándares FAIR, automatización de flujos, tableros de control y sistemas de información para MEL.
  • Experiencia demostrada en análisis de datos asociados a ecosistemas de los Andes, la Amazonía y la Orinoquía.
  • Participación como autor o coautor en publicaciones científicas, evaluaciones, síntesis de evidencia o productos de aprendizaje aplicados.
  • Experiencia trabajando en equipos interdisciplinarios y facilitando procesos de aprendizaje o fortalecimiento de capacidades con socios o comunidades.
  • Se aprecian las habilidades multilingües y la experiencia multicultural o intercultural.
  • Nivel de inglés intermedio, hablado y escrito.

Communications Director Job Description

Position: Communications Director

Location: Fully Remote (Some travel)

Reports to: Co-Director

Status: Full-time, Exempt

About BLMP

The Black LGBTQIA+ Migrant Project (BLMP) envisions a world where no one is forced to give up their homeland and where all Black LGBTQIA+ people are free and liberated. We build and center the power of Black LGBTQIA+ migrants to ensure the liberation of all Black people through Organizing & Basebuilding, Strategic Communications, and Viability & Sustainability. We are led by a directly impacted steering committee, staff and consultants, and operate organizing networks in New York City, DMV (DC, Maryland and Virginia region), Minneapolis, California, and the South. We build power, community, and knowledge in the U.S., while challenging the role that the U.S. plays globally in creating the conditions that force us to leave our homes.

Position Summary

Reporting to the Co-Director, the Director of Communications will set and guide the strategy for all communications, including digital, and public relations messages and collateral to consistently articulate BLMP’s mission. The Director of Communications will ensure that BLMP is viewed as the primary source, disseminator, and conduit of information within this diverse network and constituent base. The Director of Communications will lead the communications team, in collaboration with other staff members as the communications partner on a variety of strategic initiatives.

Responsibilities

  • Team Leadership: Supervise members of the Communications Team and lead department meetings.
  • Strategic Planning: Develop, implement, and evaluate comprehensive communications plans across the organization's diverse audiences in collaboration with BLMP’s staff team, consultants, members, and partner organizations.
  • Content & Narrative Strategy: Work closely with the Communications Strategist and Digital Organizer to lead the content strategy that engages audience segments, and build/implement narrative strategy in service of Black liberation, Black migrant justice, and abolition of the carceral state.
  • Digital & Web Presence: Mentor and lead the communications team through website administration, coordinating with the Communications Strategist to ensure new and consistent information (article links, stories, and events) are posted regularly.
  • Collateral Management: Manage development, distribution, and maintenance of all print and electronic collateral including, but not limited to, newsletters, brochures, annual reports, and website.
  • Brand & Media Relations: Strengthen BLMP brand and visual identity, create/manage media contact lists, and oversee departmental budget.
  • Rapid Response: Develop rapid response and crisis communication protocols.
  • Movement Building: Represent BLMP in communications-specific movement spaces/coalitions, infusing BLMP’s narrative strategy into the larger movement-wide narrative strategy.

Qualifications

  • Experience: At least 10 years of communications experience, ideally in an “in-house” leadership role within a nonprofit structure, covering areas such as website content, newsletters, and donor communications.
  • Strategy to Execution: Proven ability to take knowledge and transform it into exciting and useful messages, and disseminate it to the right audiences through the best distribution channels.
  • Skills: Excellent written and verbal communication skills; ability to build and incorporate organizational voice across platforms, organize/clearly share information, and stay up to date with ever-changing tools and best practices.
  • Leadership Style: Highly collaborative, mission-aligned relationship builder who welcomes and integrates feedback; a self-starter comfortable with a participatory leadership style.
  • Organization: Highly organized with the ability to manage a variety of deadline-driven initiatives concurrently.
  • Availability: Available to work nights and weekends during moments of urgent response.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Passionate about Black liberation, Black migrant justice, and abolition of the carceral state.
  • Committed to centering and building the leadership of Black migrants and 1st generation Black people who identify as TGNCI, women, femmes, and/or who are living with disabilities.
  • Bilingual.

Salary and Benefits

  • Salary: Competitive, $114,500.
  • Benefits: Comprehensive health (medical, dental, vision, and FSA)

From indie to AAA, companies partner with Xsolla to help fund, distribute, market, and monetize their games. Headquartered in Los Angeles, California, Xsolla has helped over 1,500+ game developers reach more players and grow their businesses around the world.

For more information, visit xsolla.com.

Responsibilities:

    Partner Growth & Account Management

  • Guide new publisher integrations from onboarding through launch, nurture long-term monetization partnerships, and expand existing accounts by driving adoption and incremental revenue growth through Xsolla's Offerwall.

  • Own ambiguous, cross-functional problems end-to-end — coordinating with product, engineering, and operations to identify what's broken, why, and what the right fix is, even when the answer isn't immediately obvious.
  • Anticipate downstream issues before they escalate, using pattern recognition from past partner problems to flag risks proactively rather than reactively.

    • Strategic Relationships & Executive Communication

  • Own and cultivate strategic relationships with senior and executive stakeholders at publisher partners, acting as a trusted advisor rather than a transactional point of contact.
  • Prepare and deliver executive-level business reviews, business cases, and growth roadmaps that translate complex data and problem resolutions into clear, actionable business outcomes for senior decision-makers.

Qualifications & Skills:

    Experience

    • Problem-Solving Mindset

We are seeking an exceptional Senior Director to lead and grow Turner & Townsend's advisory business across two of our most strategically important central government clients: the Home Office and Ministry of Justice.

The successful candidate will be a recognised leader within the public sector consulting market, bringing a strong track record of developing trusted executive-level relationships, securing and delivering complex advisory commissions, and leading high-performing teams through significant periods of growth. This individual will be responsible for shaping and executing client growth strategies, identifying emerging opportunities, and positioning Turner & Townsend as a trusted delivery partner across strategic transformation, programme delivery, portfolio management, operating model design and organisational change. They will work collaboratively across our advisory, programme management, commercial, digital and infrastructure businesses to bring the full breadth of our capability to clients.

Key Requirements

The ideal candidate will demonstrate:

  • A proven track record of winning and growing significant consulting and advisory revenues within the Home Office, Ministry of Justice, or closely aligned government departments and agencies.

  • Establish Turner & Townsend as a go-to advisory partner across the Home Office and Ministry of Justice.
  • Develop and maintain executive-level client relationships that translate into sustainable business growth.

  • Build and develop a high-performing team capable of supporting continued growth across government.

jobs.excerpt: Overview​ Join our Life Sciences Industry & Enterprise practice to help leading pharma, biotech, and medtech clients translate commercial ambition into executable transformation.
jobs.description:
Overview​

Join our Life Sciences Industry & Enterprise practice to help leading pharma, biotech, and medtech clients translate commercial ambition into executable transformation. This role focuses on activating commercial change across field, marketing, market access, patient services, medical, and commercial operations through operating model activation, process redesign, business requirements, technology enablement, change, and adoption.​

​

What would you do?​

As a Manager, you will lead client workstreams that move commercial strategy from design into execution. You will help clients understand how work gets done today, define how it needs to change, and build the practical plans, requirements, governance, and adoption approach needed to make transformation real.​

Your work could include:​

  • Activating commercial operating model changes across field, marketing, access, patient services, medical, and commercial operations​

  • Translating strategy into future-state processes, business requirements, user stories, decision rights, governance, and implementation plans​

  • Supporting technology-enabled transformation across CRM, content, omnichannel, patient services, workflow, analytics, and reporting platforms​

  • Identifying how AI, automation, copilots, or agentic workflows can improve commercial execution, handoffs, decision-making, and productivity​

  • Leading cross-functional workshops with business, technology, analytics, operations, change, and training stakeholders​

​

In this role you will be expected to:​

  • Anticipate risks, dependencies, and shifting client priorities; prepare teams to pivot as programs evolve while keeping delivery focused on outcomes​

  • Shape ambiguous transformation objectives into clear workplans, milestones, deliverables, and decision points​

  • Lead workstreams and manage analysts/consultants to produce client-ready outputs​

  • Manage day-to-day client relationships, including working sessions, feedback, risks, and next steps​

  • Translate commercial strategy into operating model activation, process design, business requirements, change impacts, and adoption plans​

  • Identify and govern value unlock opportunities by linking transformation activities to measurable business outcomes, value cases, KPIs, and realization plans​

  • Apply life sciences commercial knowledge to connect workflow, governance, data, technology, compliance, and talent implications​

  • Partner with technology, analytics, AI, operations, and change teams to ensure solutions are practical and executable​

  • Manage dependencies, issues, risks, stakeholder alignment, and rollout readiness across complex transformation programs​

  • Manage delivery discipline across workplans, milestones, dependencies, RAID logs, stakeholder decisions, testing / UAT needs, rollout readiness, and adoption activities​

  • Support proactive commercial transformation opportunities and proposals by shaping the client problem, workplan, solution approach, delivery model, and value story​

  • Contribute to thought capital by developing reusable perspectives, frameworks, case examples, and market-facing points of view on commercial transformation, enablement, AI/data, and future ways of working

Growth Opportunities​

You will continue to grow through:​

  • Leading commercial transformation work that turns strategy into executable change for major life sciences clients​

  • Building expertise across operating model activation, process redesign, technology enablement, AI/data, change, and adoption​

  • Partnering across Accenture teams to deliver integrated strategy, technology, operations, analytics, and change solutions​

  • Developing market-facing perspectives on commercial transformation and AI-enabled ways of working​

  • Coaching analysts and consultants into future life sciences transformation practitioners

Who do we need?​

We would love to hear from you if you have:​


Basic Qualifications:

  • Minimum of 6 years of life sciences commercial experience across one or more commercial functions: field, marketing, market access, patient services, medical, or commercial operations​
  • Minimum of 5 years of experience in strategy consulting, professional services, or an equivalent internal corporate-strategy role.
  • Bachelor's Degree

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Demonstrated ability to lead a workstream, manage clients, and coach junior team members​
  • Strong client management skills, including ability to build trusted relationships, facilitate working sessions, manage feedback, align stakeholders, and communicate risks / tradeoffs clearly​
  • Strong understanding of commercial workflows, cross-functional handoffs, governance, regulatory / compliance considerations, and capability needs​
  • Experience translating business needs into process designs, business requirements, user stories, acceptance criteria, implementation plans, or change impacts​
  • Comfort partnering across operations, technology, analytics, AI, change management, training, and business teams​
  • Experience supporting technology-enabled transformation or rollout efforts within the life sciences commercial sector​
  • Working knowledge of platforms and capabilities such as CRM, Veeva/Salesforce, content/MLR, omnichannel, patient services, reporting dashboards, workflow automation, or analytics platforms​
  • Practical understanding of AI/data-enabled transformation, including use case intake, workflow fit, data/system dependencies, guardrails, testing, adoption, measurement, and human-in-the-loop governance​
  • Proactive mindset around innovative ways of working, including how AI, automation, copilots, and agentic workflows can improve productivity, quality, collaboration, and speed of execution for external project & internal Accenture work​
  • Strong PowerPoint, Excel, facilitation, stakeholder management, written communication, and executive storytelling skills​

Position Summary:

The Portfolio Manager oversees the servicing and ongoing management of SBA, USDA, and conventional loan portfolios, ensuring full compliance with lender policies and agency regulations. This role analyzes credit risk, conducts annual reviews and servicing actions, supervises credit analysts, and facilitates communication among borrowers, lenders, and third parties, supporting loan modifications, monitoring, and documentation to protect agency guarantees and maintain portfolio performance. This position is jointly responsible for effective interaction with team members, lenders, and borrowers.

Essential Duties and Responsibilities:

  • Provide excellent and professional customer service to the borrower, lender, and governing agencies. Ensure relationships remain strong and healthy.
  • Supervise Servicing Credit Analyst (including Decimal Point), review all financial spreads and narratives prepared by them, and ensure quality assurance of SBA/USDA credit files prior to audits and regulatory reviews.
  • Review borrower service requests, gather necessary information, and underwrite servicing actions—including modifications, annual loan reviews, and amendments such as collateral releases, pricing adjustments, risk-rating changes, and other necessary modifications—in accordance with lender policies, agency regulations, SOPs, and CFR.
  • Manage all aspects of portfolio management for SBA, USDA, Main Street, and conventional loans according to lender credit policy and SBA/USDA procedures, including portfolio monitoring, collections on past due accounts, collection of financial documentation, annual reviews, servicing actions, and communication with the SBA/USDA.
  • Collaborate with legal counsel, lenders, borrowers, and third parties on credit actions and servicing requests, including loan modifications, annual reviews, and documentation exception management; engage with all parties both verbally and in writing.
  • Complete comprehensive narrative annual reviews for each existing SBA/USDA loan, including business and personal financial analysis, credit analysis, lien perfection, property valuation, industry comparisons, risk identification and mitigation, and loan grading recommendations.
  • Order and review third-party reports such as real estate appraisals, environmental assessments, title reports, and business equipment valuations as required.
  • Ensure proper implementation of LSP, lender, and SBA/USDA business policies and procedures, and promote adherence to regulatory compliance requirements.
  • Maintain and manage financial and insurance ticklers, collect statements and policies, prepare SBA/USDA loan files for regulatory or agency audits, and fulfill all portfolio management responsibilities—including collections and communications between the lender and the SBA/USDA, and oversight of portfolio management expenses.
  • Participate in special projects and support the SBA/USDA servicing department as needed, including assisting borrowers with servicing actions and tracking financial, insurance, and covenant requirements.
  • Oversee the transition of a troubled loan to the Special Asset Portfolio Manager’s portfolio. Provide on going assistance as needed.

Primary Success Measurements:

  • Continue to improve individual performance, with a goal of processing 9-12 actions a month
  • Improve quality of credit analysis as needed.
  • Respond to external customer emails, correspondence and phone calls in a timely manner (24-48 hours.)

Education and/or Experience:

Knowledge and/or Skills:

  • Knowledge of the SBA and USDA rules and regulations, preferred.
  • Strong credit skills.
  • Leadership and motivational skills, good written and verbal communication skills, decision-making and analytical skills and ability to work well under pressure.
  • Operate other standard office equipment; type accurately at a speed necessary to meet the requirements of the position; organize work, set priorities and exercise sound independent judgment within established guidelines; interpret, apply, explain and reach sound decisions.

Mathematical Skills:

This individual will be responsible for designing, building, testing, and supporting healthcare integrations connecting clinical software platforms with electronic medical records (EMR) and oncology information systems. The role will work across HL7, FHIR, REST APIs, interface engines, cloud infrastructure, and clinical data workflows to ensure accurate and reliable exchange of patient and treatment information.

The ideal candidate will have strong hands-on experience with healthcare interfaces, data mapping and transformation, and troubleshooting complex integration issues across multiple systems. This individual will also work directly with hospital and healthcare IT teams during implementations, testing, and production go-lives.

This is a fully remote position within the United States, with occasional travel of approximately 10–15% to customer sites for onboarding and go-live support.

Responsibilities

  • Design, build, configure, and support HL7 and FHIR interfaces connecting healthcare applications with EMR and clinical information systems.
  • Analyze source and target data models and develop detailed mapping and transformation logic for clinical and treatment data.
  • Build and maintain interface engine configurations using platforms such as Mirth Connect, Rhapsody, Cloverleaf, Corepoint, or similar technologies.
  • Troubleshoot interface failures, malformed messages, acknowledgment errors, mapping issues, and data integrity problems by tracing transactions across the full integration path.
  • Develop and maintain interface specifications, data mapping documentation, test plans, and technical runbooks.
  • Support integration services running in AWS and containerized environments, including Kubernetes and Docker, while monitoring logs, metrics, and system health.
  • Plan and execute unit, integration, and user-acceptance testing to validate data accuracy and system functionality prior to production deployment.
  • Collaborate directly with hospital and healthcare IT teams, implementation teams, software engineers, product teams, and third-party integration resources during customer onboarding and go-live activities.
  • Develop reusable integration templates, mapping standards, and implementation practices to improve the consistency and efficiency of future customer integrations.
  • Support clinical data integrations while maintaining appropriate handling of protected health information (PHI) and healthcare compliance requirements.

Requirements

  • 5+ years of hands-on experience in healthcare interface or integration engineering, ideally within EMR, oncology, imaging, or other clinical technology environments.
  • Strong working knowledge of HL7 v2.x messaging, including ADT, ORM, ORU, and SIU messages.
  • Familiarity with HL7 v3/CDA, FHIR R4, and RESTful APIs.
  • Hands-on experience building or supporting integrations with major EMR platforms, particularly Epic; exposure to Cerner or similar systems is also valuable.
  • Experience with healthcare interface engines such as Mirth Connect, Rhapsody, Cloverleaf, Corepoint, or similar platforms.
  • Strong experience with clinical data mapping and transformation across disparate systems, including coded values, units, identifiers, and other healthcare data elements.
  • Working knowledge of AWS and containerized environments, including Docker and Kubernetes.
  • Strong troubleshooting skills with the ability to read logs, trace messages end-to-end, and identify root causes across multiple systems and teams.

  • Experience with oncology, radiation oncology, treatment planning, or clinical workflow systems is highly preferred.
  • HL7, FHIR, AWS, or other relevant technical certification is a plus.
  • Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Information Technology, or a related technical field is preferred.
  • Ability to work core U.S. business hours, with occasional early or late meetings to collaborate with international engineering teams.

The Technical Lead is the senior architect and technical role in AiVA engagements. Once a client engagement is signed, this role owns the architectural pattern, the integration approach, and the technical quality of everything the AiVA pod builds. The role provides architectural direction, technical review, and escalation resolution. Accountable not for building skills but for the technical soundness of what gets built and liaising with the platform engineering team where necessary.

Overall Aims:

  • Technical architecture that supports the engagement outcomes: scalable, maintainable, secure, and defensible under client technical scrutiny.
  • Consistent architectural pattern across the assigned pods.
  • Sound technical decisions within the engagement, with clear architectural guidance to the AI Workflow Engineers.
  • Technical soundness that supports both immediate engagement outcomes and long-term client platform investment.
  • Architectural clarity that lets AI Workflow Engineers build at pace without technical rework.

Architecture & Technical Direction

  • Define the architectural pattern for each engagement: skill decomposition, tool orchestration, data flow, integration approach, and deployment model.
  • Ensure all architecture patterns are in line with security best practices and with client requirements. Designing client specific guardrails as appropriate
  • Review and sign off on AI Workflow Engineer builds against the agreed architectural pattern.
  • Own integration architecture with client systems: authentication, data ingress, downstream deployment, and monitoring.
  • Make platform-versus-custom decisions with the Head of Platform Engineering and Product where the engagement stretches platform capability.
  • Design and document the target technical state, transition plan, and operational readiness criteria for handover to sustained delivery.
  • Own the technical risk register for the engagement; surface and escalate technical risks early to the Delivery Principal.

Engagement Execution

  • Work across multiple client engagements as the Technical Lead.

  • Guide the AI Workflow Engineer on architectural choices, prompt strategy, and evaluation design without taking over the build.

Technical Leadership

  • Develop and mentor AI Workflow Engineers and Integration Engineers through the engagement; provide structured technical input to functional managers on capability development.

Continuous Improvement & Standards

  • Contribute architectural patterns and technical playbooks to the Technical Lead community; refine standards based on engagement experience.

  • Deep interest in AI-enabled automation architecture; keeps up with the platform, integration patterns, and the wider AI engineering community.

  • Comfortable working across geographies (US, UK, India) and across sectors including legal and professional services.

jobs.excerpt: About Ursa Health We're Ursa Health, an 11-year-old, growth stage company.
jobs.description:
About Ursa Health

We're Ursa Health, an 11-year-old, growth stage company. We straddle the line between being a software company and a tech-enabled consultancy, turning healthcare data into actionable insights. We've developed our healthcare data platform over the last decade combining deep industry IP with a flexible and powerful software product. Thanks to our unique, methodical approach, we're able to make sense of data in a way nobody else in the industry is able to – generating analytics that are trusted enough to change how care is delivered.

We're not talking about fancy black-box models or AI agents, although we do that too. Simply the work of taking healthcare data in its messy, raw format and turning it into results that accurately describe what is actually happening to patients; very few organizations can do this well. And, because of that, we serve as the core data and analytics engine for many of the most innovative companies in healthcare.

We're growing our team and are looking for engineers who can straddle this line between a software company and a consultancy. It's in our DNA that the people building our software products should also be on the front line of client-facing work. It's a hybrid role, and you'll have to be comfortable billing hourly on idiosyncratic client deliverables. But you'll also be channeling that work back into our software products, including our longstanding Ursa Studio and our newer AI-assisted tools like Compass and Sentinel.

Ursa Health is fully remote. We've been fully remote since our founding and have a strong remote-only culture. Hours are flexible. You'll be able – and indeed expected – to turn off Slack for hours at a time in order to get into a flow to solve the most difficult problems.

We believe in a very human application process — and are leaning further into this given the volume of AI-generated and fraudulent applications we're seeing across the industry. If you want to apply to join our team, submit your complete application including current personal contact information, an updated LinkedIn profile, and an updated CV. Qualified candidates will be asked to submit a 2-minute intro video and complete a technical puzzle, which shouldn't take more than a couple hours. The puzzle is drawn straight from our work and will give you an honest sense of the real-life challenges you'll be expected to tackle. After that, you'll interview with our team. We look forward to learning about your experience, getting to know you as a person, and giving you a real window into life at Ursa.

We're excited to meet candidates who are already authorized to work in the U.S., as we are currently unable to provide visa sponsorship.

Ursa Health is an equal opportunity employer. We are passionate about achieving diversity on our team because we know that different backgrounds and points of view fuel innovation and creativity, and will therefore help us reach our goal of making healthcare better and more equitable for all. We foster an inclusive environment where we can celebrate our differences. We encourage candidates from diverse backgrounds to apply to this and all of our open positions. All applicants will be considered for employment without consideration of race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, disability, veteran status, or any other status protected by applicable law.

About the Role

Role Department: Delivery

Reports to: AVP, Integration Engineering

The Data Integration Engineer role is ideal for an experienced data professional eager to put their healthcare domain knowledge and engineering expertise to work in a collaborative, mission-driven environment. Your efforts to organize, transform, and automate the flow of healthcare data will unlock actionable insights for our clients, enabling them to move from raw data to meaningful analysis in hours rather than weeks. You'll interpret and integrate client data claims, ADT, clinical/EMR, provider billing, and other operational datasets into the Ursa Core Data Model, building reusable, enduring data models that clients rely on to drive clinical, operational, and financial decisions.

You will work closely with Ursa colleagues across analytics engineering, product development, and customer success, as well as directly with client teams including data architects, analysts, clinicians, and other healthcare professionals to understand their data and their needs. You'll leverage Ursa Health's data platform to design and build integration pipelines, data models and increasingly, work alongside AI-assisted tooling that accelerates the process.

About You

  • You're looking for a role that will allow you to apply your experience to a "blank canvas" to design and create elegant and enduring data models.
  • You have great attention to detail and enjoy the process of investigating and interpreting raw data. You anticipate dataset-specific inconsistencies and edge cases before they become problems.
  • You are a consultative partner by nature, comfortable working directly with a range of stakeholders (clinical, operational, data/technology, and actuarial) to understand how data was generated, what its limitations are, and how it will be used.
  • You are looking to join a collaborative team that is passionate about healthcare and strives to build best in class healthcare analytics.
  • You're curious by nature and excited to use technologies that allow you more time to explore, test, and iterate on the data model you design rather than worry about maintaining fragile code.
  • You have a deep understanding of health information systems, medical claims and/or billing data across payors and/or clinical data from your experience as a data architect and/or engineer.
  • You balance technical rigor with pragmatic elegance building solutions that are durable without being overcomplicated.
  • You've worked with AI tools and have developed a clear-eyed sense of where they help and where they don't especially in a domain where the cost of a wrong answer is high.

Responsibilities

  • Lead the integration of complex healthcare data packages including medical claims, pharmacy claims, revenue cycle billing, ADT, clinical/EMR, FHIR and value-based care financial datasets into custom or Ursa Studio standard data models through collaboration with client and Ursa Health teams.
  • Design and operationalize rigorous validation checks that preserve data integrity, prevent analytics degradation, and maintain client trust.
  • Communicate with clients to understand their data, its limitations, and intended analytical use cases to support them in interpreting the findings that drive their businesses.
  • Effectively communicate with internal and client teams to gather and understand the information necessary to successfully complete projects, documenting both the process and final deliverables so a non-technical stakeholder can understand the interpretation and business rules.
  • Collaborate with analytics engineers, customer success, and product teams to align delivery with client expectations and to surface product opportunities informed by client needs and data behavior.
  • Support client teams to advance their implementation initiatives, including training, measure building, and report interpretation.
  • Thoughtfully leverage AI-assisted tooling to accelerate and improve delivery, applying domain knowledge and human judgment to ensure sound output.
  • Keep your knowledge current regarding data security and privacy procedures and policies. Comply with HIPAA procedures and collaborate with the Incident Response Team as directed.

Qualifications

Required 

  • Bachelor’s degree
  • 4+ years of experience working with healthcare financial (e.g., claims, provider billing data), clinical or pharmacy data domains
  • Familiarity with healthcare data integration concepts, common data sources (payer data files, EMR/EHR systems), data formats (claims, billing, X12 835/837/270, HL7 ADT, FHIR), and medical coding standards (CPT, ICD-10)
  • 4+ years implementing and maintaining ETL/ELT pipelines and processes. 
  • 4+ years of experience in end-to-end data integration (data discovery, data cleansing and curation, analysis, transformation, validation and maintenance). 
  • High proficiency working with SQL, relational database systems (e.g., Snowflake, Microsoft SQL, Oracle, PostgreSQL) and data modeling. 
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills. 

Preferred 

  • Knowledgeable in healthcare interoperability / integration engines
  • Experience with ELT or workflow orchestration tools such as Fivetran, dbt, Dagster, or Airflow. While this role applies those concepts within Ursa Studio rather than using those tools directly, the ability to think in systems is a plus.
  • Experience building data models that support healthcare outcome measurement.
  • Familiarity with value-based care data and financial models.
  • Working understanding of Python or JavaScript to manipulate and transform large datasets and data science fundamentals.
  • Experience working with AI tools in a professional context, with the judgment to apply them appropriately in healthcare data environments where output accuracy is critical.
  • History of working with remote teams.

Location

  • United States, Position is Remote

At Included Health, the Associate Clinical Director, Integrated Care Quality (NP/MD) is responsible for the strategy, external representation, and program leadership needed to ensure our clinical services perform credibly in high-stakes client, consultant, and audit-facing settings.

This role leads the clinical quality approach to client audits, consultant engagement, and longitudinal quality assurance across relevant services. The Director will represent Included Health in consequential meetings with clients, consultants, health plans, and internal leaders; shape the vision for external-facing clinical quality work; build trusted relationships; and translate audit and quality findings into durable operational improvement strategies.

Establishing a robust longitudinal oversight process is a primary objective for this position. This leader will drive the development of systems to monitor member journeys, ensure care quality, and maintain service reliability over time. Furthermore, they will utilize AI-driven quality surveillance and pattern detection to modernize and scale quality operations.

Responsibilities

  • Represent Included Health clinical services in high-stakes client, consultant, and audit-related discussions.

  • Build strong relationships with clients, consultants, health plans, and internal commercial partners.

We are seeking a hands-on, self-starting Technical Marketing Engineer (TME) with deep networking expertise to drive technical enablement, customer validation, and field readiness for our next-generation Zero Trust Branch solutions. In this high-impact role, you will architect and maintain complex lab environments, lead hands-on Proof of Value (PoV) customer engagements, and provide technical troubleshooting to resolve escalations.   • Architect, Build, and Maintain Advanced Lab Topologies by designing, deploying, and maintaining resilient physical and virtual networking lab environments simulating complex enterprise branch, edge, retail network topologies to rigorously test product behavior, interoperability, and real-world scale

  • Drive Complex Technical Troubleshooting & Escalation Resolution by serving as the direct technical escalation bridge between field teams and core engineering to diagnose, reproduce, and resolve critical L2/L3 networking escalations, network segmentation challenges, and packet-level anomalies during active customer pilots

  • Author Technical Documentation, Deployment Guides, and Reference Architectures by developing production-ready technical collateral, including step-by-step deployment runbooks, reference architectures, white papers, competitive test plans, and solution briefs to standardize best practices and accelerate post-sales time-to-value

  • Deliver Field Readiness & Enablement Training by creating and conducting high-impact technical training programs, interactive workshops, and technical webinars for Systems Engineers (SEs), professional services, and channel partner architects to scale deployment self-sufficiency across distributed enterprise environments

Who You Are (Success Profile)

  • Operate with a strong ownership mindset, combining a passion for the mission with high integrity and the ability to navigate seamlessly between strategic planning and hands-on execution.

  • Maintain a customer-obsessed approach, building deep empathy for internal and external stakeholders to solve real-world problems and champion their success.

  • Move with a strong sense of urgency, focusing on execution and delivering high-impact, high-quality results rapidly in a growth-oriented environment.

  • Drive innovation through deep curiosity, enjoying complex technical challenges and leveraging technology to build secure, scalable solutions.

  • Lead with integrity and accountability, consistently aligning actions with words to build trust across teams.

What We’re Looking for (Minimum Qualifications)

  • Demonstrated curiosity and active exploration of AI tools, with a proven history of integrating new technologies to enhance daily workflows and augment problem-solving

  • 5+ years of hands-on experience in technical marketing, solutions architecture, or advanced systems engineering with deep subject matter expertise in enterprise routing, switching, TCP/IP, L2/L3 network segmentation, and tunneling protocols (WireGuard, IPsec, VxLAN)

  • Proven track record of leading and winning hands-on customer Proof of Value (PoV) pilots and executive architectural evaluations within complex enterprise and distributed edge networking environments

  • Hands-on proficiency in building and maintaining multi-vendor physical and virtual network lab topologies using bare-metal appliances, hypervisors (ESXi, KVM), and network emulation platforms (EVE-NG, GNS3)

  • Advanced packet analysis and troubleshooting expertise using Wireshark, tcpdump, and traffic generation tools to diagnose real-time routing anomalies, latency/jitter, MTU issues, and NAT/firewall traversal

  • Demonstrated track record of authoring production-grade technical collateral (deployment runbooks, reference architectures, white papers) and delivering technical enablement sessions to sales engineering, professional services, and partner teams

What Will Make You Stand Out (Preferred Qualifications)

  • Proven ability to leverage AI technologies and workflows to drive measurable operational efficiency

  • Practical experience with Python, Bash scripting, or infrastructure-as-code and configuration management tools (e.g., Ansible, Terraform, REST APIs) to automate lab deployment, test execution, and repetitive networking workflows

  • Working knowledge of public cloud networking architectures (AWS VPCs/Transit Gateways, Azure Virtual WAN, GCP Cloud Routers) or container networking environments (Docker, Kubernetes) connecting distributed branch edges to cloud workloads

  • Recognized networking or security certifications (e.g., CCIE/CCNP Enterprise or Security, JNCIP, PCNSE) or direct architectural experience with retail, kiosk, IoT/OT, or cellular WAN/5G failover deployments

jobs.excerpt: TEECOM hires by discipline, not by open requisition.
jobs.description:
TEECOM hires by discipline, not by open requisition. We are growing — multiple teams across the US, UK, and India are actively hiring to grow their teams.

When you apply here, you are applying to TEECOM for a role in Technical Project Management. Rather than interviewing for a single posted role, you will go through a structured Discipline Assessment that establishes your level and demonstrated capability. Once your level is determined, TEECOM's recruiting and leadership teams match your profile to the best available opening on a team that fits your skills, experience, and goals.

Roles span Technical Project Manager I through Technical Project Manager III. Your level — and your title — are determined by your assessment, not by the role you apply to.

If you have meaningful experience in more than one discipline, apply to your primary discipline and tell your recruiter about your secondary discipline(s) during your Introduction Call. You may be scheduled for a separate Discipline Assessment for each one.

Technical Project Management at TEECOM

    Technical Project Managers at TEECOM are the primary point of contact for client accounts — they own the relationship, the technology scope, and the delivery across multiple concurrent projects. This is a client-facing, field-active role: TPMs spend significant time on-site managing the technology scope of active projects alongside construction teams, contractors, and client stakeholders.

    TPMs are not pure project managers — they bring genuine technical depth in at least one discipline (ICT/Telecom, Security, AV, Wireless, or similar) and use that expertise to make real-time decisions in the field, review deliverables for quality, and maintain client trust through construction and commissioning. Work spans managing design team coordination, leading client meetings, driving construction administration, reviewing submittals and RFIs, and ensuring projects close out cleanly.

    At more senior levels, Technical Project Managers take ownership of major accounts with multiple active projects, mentor junior TPMs and engineers, and contribute to growing the account and TEECOM's presence with the client.

What We're Looking For

    We hire at all levels — the strongest Technical Project Managers are proactive, coachable, and take ownership of client relationships and outcomes: they're as comfortable with a stakeholder as they are in the field, they don't wait for problems to find them, they own the commercial and technical outcomes of every project they run, and they're always thinking about what comes next — growing the partnership, not just closing the project.

    If you don’t have everything on this list yet, that’s expected — TEECOM develops people through structured documentation, mentorship, and real project work.

    • Technical background in at least one technology discipline (ICT/Telecom, Security, AV, Wireless, or similar) — you can review drawings, discuss design decisions, and troubleshoot issues in the field
    • Experience managing technology consulting or AEC projects through the full lifecycle — design, construction administration, and commissioning
    • Comfort being on-site regularly — this role requires field presence across active projects
    • Client-facing ownership — you manage the relationship directly and are accountable for project outcomes
    • Strong commercial and financial management skills — managing scope, contracts, budgets, schedules, and risk
    • Strong technical communication skills — you translate technical issues into clear decisions and coordinate across disciplines, clients, and contractors
    • Experience managing multiple concurrent projects across a single client account or portfolio
    • Degree in any four-year engineering discipline, construction project management, technology management, or a related technical field — or equivalent hands-on experience
    • PMP certification or equivalent — preferred

      • *TEECOM covers exam fees and study materials for certifications relevant to your discipline, pays a one-time bonus when you pass, and funds all continuing education — including conference attendance.

TEECOM is a fully remote consulting firm. We hire across all US states, the UK, and India. Our projects span the globe — some roles involve international travel, so share your comfort level with your recruiter.
